YOUR EMPHASIS (turn 1), different from a sibling doing fix-by-fix conformance:

1. **PATCH-READINESS above all** — this is the last gun aimed at production. Audit run_patch end to end as if you must sign off personally: source_links(artefact) composition over the REAL artefact (compose them, count non-empty, spot-check 20 against the published tree byte-for-byte); the count precondition (namespace holds 1,337,009 after the twin cleanup — the artefact composes exactly that many? verify); checkpoint semantics under every interruption point (crash before first checkpoint, mid-group, after last; then resume; then rerun-after-complete); the schema included with patch_rows (source_link string filterable False — is sending schema on every batch correct per turbopuffer docs? any risk of schema conflict with the EXISTING namespace schema uploaded at export time — the namespace already has source_link? NO it does not — the column was added to namespace_schema in site_export but the LIVE namespace was exported BEFORE that change; verify what happens when patch introduces a new attribute + schema on a namespace whose stored schema lacks it); the _count() None-handling if aggregations missing; BATCH_WORKERS import; PATCH_ROWS=4096 × ~120B rows vs request limits; idempotency of re-patching; rate limits / retry behavior via site_export.request's _RETRY_STATUS on patch failures mid-group. Simulate with a stub what you can; WebFetch the write docs for what you cannot. Name every residual risk explicitly, however small, and give the exact patch invocation you would run (flags, checkpoint path) plus the post-patch verification (gate --namespace: stratified sample semantics — verify _gate_namespace_sample would pass against a correctly patched namespace and fail against a half-patched one, given the id In filter's behavior with 500 ids and include_attributes; is 'rank_by id asc + top_k len(chosen) + filter In' guaranteed to return ALL chosen rows?).
2. **Regression hunt in the delta**: the v3 rewrite touched publish's whole body (build_relocation, size verification, css counting, index counting, report-in-staging, BaseException cleanup) and the gate's whole body (two buckets, promised-pages assert, counter equality, artefact-hash binding). Look for: the size-verification loop hitting every relocation rel BEFORE staging exists (cost? double-getsize?); BaseException catch swallowing KeyboardInterrupt semantics (rmtree then re-raise — is staging removal on Ctrl-C acceptable per "removes its own staging"?); report written inside staging then os.rename — but artefact_hash stamped from load — fine?; gate's promised-pages loop building aux_page(sym) for 1,139 syms + fonts basenames — any duplicate/missing vs files walk; the '9870 page(s)' log arithmetic; positioned-coverage division by zero when no records.
3. **The merge rework on real data**: re-run merge_aux_copies over the real tree's 22 multi-copy groups (read from the rendered tree) and diff the outputs against what publish actually wrote into ~/isasearch-published/_aux — byte-identical? The base-selection: for each of the 12 conflicting groups, which copy won and is its title the symbolic one?
4. **The D54 split's blind spot hunt**: can a fragment miss that is genuinely OUR fault be misclassified as inherited (e.g. our rewrite mangles a fragment — fragments are never touched by rewrite_html_refs... verify byte-preservation of fragments through the rewrite on real pages); the inherited_misses cap-free list memory; the "verified on N pages" arithmetic.
5. **ELEGANCE**: any dirty hack that slipped into the fix batch under time pressure; invariants-by-convention remaining.

Mark borderline-pedantic candidates LOW/pedantic explicitly. Label spec-relaxation proposals separately. Return a ranked numbered findings list (severity, file:line, one-sentence defect, concrete failure scenario, fix direction), then a dedicated PATCH-READINESS verdict section (GO / GO-with-amendments / NO-GO, with the exact command and post-checks). Verify every finding against actual code/artifacts; no generic advice.

- connect-mbzuai-fm: How to SSH into the mbzuai-fm login node and run remote commands so that conda/python (and tools like manage_data.py, huggingface_hub, isabelle) are actually available. Use whenever running any non-trivial command on mbzuai-fm — the default non-interactive SSH shell has NO conda, NO python, and NO zsh on PATH, so commands silently fail with "command not found" unless wrapped in a login+interactive shell. Covers the local `mfm` helper and the quoting-proof stdin `"$(cat)"` trick for commands containing quotes / awk / $(...).
- doc-coauthoring: Guide users through a structured workflow for co-authoring documentation. Use when user wants to write documentation, proposals, technical specs, decision docs, or similar structured content. This workflow helps users efficiently transfer context, refine content through iteration, and verify the doc works for readers. Trigger when user mentions writing docs, creating proposals, drafting specs, or similar documentation tasks.
- aoa-putnam-eval: Reusable pipeline to evaluate the AoA agent (driver DeepSeek.V4-pro by default) over PutnamBench via Isa-REPL, and to continuously audit the per-case logs for AoA-agent defects. Use when the user wants to run/resume the AoA-on-PutnamBench evaluation, bring up its RPC-host+REPL servers, triage the agent logs, or maintain the AoA defect report.
- isabelle-datatype: How to read constants and theorems generated by Isabelle datatype and codatatype definitions
- isabelle-intro-elim-rules: How to read Isabelle introduction and elimination rules
- isabelle-ML: Essential reference for all Isabelle/ML development — system library, data structures, exception handling, and coding patterns. Load this skill whenever writing or modifying Isabelle/ML code.
- isabelle-ml-style: Isabelle/ML coding style guide and conventions based on official implementation documentation
- isabelle-proof-tool-development: Techniques for developing proof tools in Isabelle, including understanding HHF (Hereditary Harrop Formula) proof state representation
- isabelle-record: How to read constants and theorems generated by Isabelle record definitions
- isabelle-scala-plugin: How to write Isabelle/Scala plugins (Scala.Fun) that ML can call via PIDE protocol
- locale-interpretation-duplicate-fact: Fix "*** Duplicate fact declaration ... occurred while activating facts of locale instance" that aborts a concrete `interpretation`/`sublocale`/`global_interpretation` in batch `isabelle build` (but only warns in interactive jEdit). Happens when the interpreted locale's inheritance chain declares the SAME short fact name in two different ancestor locales. Use when an interpretation of a deep locale hierarchy (e.g. IsaGeoCoq's Tarski_* chain) fails on fact activation with duplicate names.
- mathbench-import-reconcile: Playbook for adding a new import to MathBench_ProverBase and reconciling any syntax conflicts (constant/type short-name resolution and notation) so that PutnamBench problems still parse to identical goal terms. Use when adding/changing imports of the MathBench_Prover session, or when investigating MathBench-vs-PutnamBench environment divergences.
- missing-lemma-loop: Operational pipeline to start, monitor, STOP, and recover the MathBench missing-lemma loop running in multi-node fleet mode on the MBZUAI cluster (watcher + slurmx fleet REPLs + login-node RPC host + serial adjudication + phase-2 import reconciliation). Use when launching/resuming the fleet run, stopping it cleanly, recovering after a crash, or applying the hard-won operational rules (correct kill sequence, git safety on the shared checkout, shell/conda/timeout fixes, re-collection prerequisite). For the single-machine AoA×PutnamBench eval use `aoa-putnam-eval` instead; for the design rationale of the loop see `MISSING_LEMMA_LOOP.md`.
- sync-isabelle-afp-distribution: How to repackage/upload and download/unpack the Isabelle + paired AFP distribution, published together as contrib/Isabelle2025-2_and_afp-2026-05-13.tar.zst on the Hugging Face Hub (via manage_data.py update/get). Use when publishing a rebuilt Isabelle+AFP tarball (after isabelle scala_build, patches, etc.) or installing/refreshing the distribution on another machine.
- sync-semantic-embedding-db: How to install or refresh the semantic embedding database (LMDB stores at ~/.cache/Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding; layered — a read-only system DB under the writable user DB). The development channel is the Hugging Face Hub tarball via manage_data.py (get/update). End users instead install the system DB from the conda channel (the isabelle-semantic-data package, or `isabelle-semantics pull`). Use when setting up or refreshing the semantic DB on a machine, or when deformalizations / vector stores are stale or missing. Do NOT dispatch `isabelle-semantics release` — publishing is a human-only action.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Author: Qiyuan Xu <xqyww123@gmail.com>

    §17 v3: the second review round's fixes, and rulings Q3-Q6 — 109 unit tests
    
    The three blockers, each reproduced on real data by the reviewers:
    - invert_theories no longer infers the distribution root from a '/src/'
      split (four Naproche component theories broke it): AFP prefix from
      /thys/, distribution prefix as the literal common string prefix, and
      the real invariant asserted — every path starts with exactly one of
      the two prefixes.  map gains --repo-root for the B3 source reads.
    - merge_aux_copies implements D49 ruling 6 as amended: tolerance is
      line-for-line text equality with <title>/<h1> set aside (admits the
      three measured conflict shapes), the base copy is the one whose title
      names the symbolic path, and the caller rewrites the merged content in
      the BASE copy's directory context.
    - The gate reads a target only when a non-empty fragment points into it
      (the 13 binary fonts are never opened as UTF-8), and a fragment into a
      non-markup target is a failure, not a traceback.
    
    The identity chain, all five links: theories.json sha256 + registry
    fingerprint + the full {file: size} tree inventory sealed in the
    artefact (Q3 — D51's dangling decision now reads the sealed set, the
    filesystem probe and the root-absolute escape are gone, and publish
    verifies each file's size as it reads it); the publish report carries
    the artefact hash and the gate refuses a mismatched pair; the export
    checkpoint pins the source-links digest like the patch checkpoint
    always did.
    
    The alarm discipline made comparable and compared: CSS externals are
    counted once (not per rendered copy), the generated index passes
    through the same counting, the D51 counter counts anchors, and the
    gate fails when its own external count differs from the report's.
    Also: the export refuses a missing artefact before any network action
    and refuses the contradictory flag pair (--dump included, ruled Q5);
    the gate asserts every classification-promised page is served (the
    generated index being the one page nothing else references) and prints
    the positioned coverage; the cross-check treats unresolvable declaring
    hashes as absence of evidence; build_relocation is the one walk over
    the classification with per-class collision arity and the generated
    paths pre-claimed; classify_reference/line_fragment/line_mark state the
    shared conventions once; publish-report.json ships publicly with raw
    rendered paths (Q6 exemption).
    
    109 tests pass; full-suite regression clean (the 10 pre-existing
    failures are the untouched interpretation-driver area).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

    D54 (user-approved): the gate's zero-miss splits by fragment provenance
    
    The first real gate run found 106 dangling fragments — all offset_…
    references the renderer emitted without ever anchoring the target id,
    verified present in the rendered input.  Ruled: a fragment this pipeline
    composed or injected (row links' #L<n>, needed marks) misses at zero
    tolerance; a fragment inherited from the rendered pages is still checked
    but a miss is counted and reported — the alarm family's third standing
    number, baseline 106 — because an inherited miss lands the reader at the
    top of the right page (D47's silent harmless degradation) and blocking
    publication on the renderer's own omission would park the pipeline
    behind an upstream bug forever.  §17.5 amended; a fragment into a
    binary target likewise reports for inherited references and fails for
    composed ones.  109 tests pass.

383	   383	def invert_theories(theories: dict) -> 'tuple[dict[str, str], dict[str, str]]':
384	   384	    """`(path → long name, the two tree prefixes)` from `data/theories.json`.
385	   385	
386	   386	    Folds the `(global)`-alias twins first — `X.X` beside `X` with the same
387	   387	    path is the session-qualified alias of a global theory (the same fold
388	   388	    `data/isabelle.py` applies at load; stated twice because this module must
389	   389	    run from a bare checkout on cslh19).  The inversion must be injective:
390	   390	    two long names on one path after the fold is a hard error, not a pick.
391	   391	
392	   392	    The prefixes are detected from the table itself: every path sits under
393	   393	    exactly one of two roots — the AFP snapshot (the one containing `/thys/`)
394	   394	    and the distribution."""
395	   395	    aliases = set()
396	   396	    for a in theories:
397	   397	        if "." in a:
398	   398	            b = a.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
399	   399	            if (a == f"{b}.{b}" and b in theories
400	   400	                    and theories[b]["path"] == theories[a]["path"]):
401	   401	                aliases.add(a)
402	   402	    inverted: 'dict[str, str]' = {}
403	   403	    for name, info in theories.items():
404	   404	        if name in aliases:
405	   405	            continue
406	   406	        path = info["path"]
407	   407	        if path in inverted:
408	   408	            raise SourcePagesError(
409	   409	                f"theories.json maps both {inverted[path]!r} and {name!r} to "
410	   410	                f"{path!r} — the inversion must be injective")
411	   411	        inverted[path] = name
412	   412	
413	   413	    # The AFP root is the prefix up to `/thys/` (no distribution path contains
414	   414	    # that segment — measured); the distribution root is the literal common
415	   415	    # string prefix of everything else, cut at its last `/` — NOT
416	   416	    # `posixpath.commonpath`, which normalises the leading `./` away.  The
417	   417	    # check below is the invariant `normalize_position` actually needs, not a
418	   418	    # proxy: every path must start with exactly one of the two prefixes.
419	   419	    # (Distribution components live under `contrib/`, not `src/` — the four
420	   420	    # Naproche theories are the measured case a `/src/` split would break.)
421	   421	    afp_set = {p[:p.index("/thys/") + len("/thys/")]
422	   422	               for p in inverted if "/thys/" in p}
423	   423	    if len(afp_set) != 1:
424	   424	        raise SourcePagesError(
425	   425	            f"theories.json's AFP paths sit under {len(afp_set)} roots: "
426	   426	            f"{sorted(afp_set)}")
427	   427	    afp = afp_set.pop()
428	   428	    home_paths = [p for p in inverted if "/thys/" not in p]
429	   429	    common = os.path.commonprefix(home_paths)
430	   430	    home = common[:common.rindex("/") + 1] if "/" in common else ""
431	   431	    bad = [p for p in inverted
432	   432	           if p.startswith(afp) == p.startswith(home) or not (
433	   433	               p.startswith(afp) or p.startswith(home))]
434	   434	    if not home or bad:
435	   435	        raise SourcePagesError(
436	   436	            f"theories.json paths do not partition under two roots "
437	   437	            f"(afp={afp!r}, home={home!r}); offending: {bad[:5]}")
438	   438	    return inverted, {"$AFP/": afp, "~~/": home}

1	r"""The source-page upload pass (SEMANTIC_SEARCH_SITE_PLAN.md §17): the rendered
     2	tree becomes the published tree, and every namespace row gains its finished
     3	source link.
     4	
     5	Five steps, run as subcommands, on the machines §17.1 assigns them to:
     6	
     7	* **scan** — the corpus scan, on the machine with the semantic DB: walks exactly
     8	  the record set the site export publishes (`site_export.iter_shippable`, one
     9	  filter chain for both) and writes the per-record position triples plus the
    10	  declaring-theory evidence the map's cross-check consumes.
    11	* **map** — on cslh19, beside the rendered tree, the authoritative registry and
    12	  the source trees: derives every rendered page's theory long name (D52),
    13	  builds the file→page map by one lookup over `data/theories.json` (D53, with
    14	  the three staleness gates and the declaring-hash zero-conflict cross-check),
    15	  and seals classification, map and positions into **one artefact whose
    16	  content hash every later step re-checks** — no step ever reads "whichever
    17	  table this machine happens to have".
    18	* **publish** — the pass itself (§17.4), on cslh19: relocates the kept pages
    19	  under their long names, rewrites every site-internal reference, passes
    20	  site-external references through byte-identically (D50), strips
    21	  input-dangling anchors with a WARNING each (D51), injects the needed line
    22	  marks, merges the conflicting auxiliary copies by id-union (D49 ruling 6),
    23	  and generates the index and the one stylesheet — all into a fresh directory
    24	  atomically renamed into place, removed again if the pass fails, and never a
    25	  directory it was handed.
    26	* **gate** — the link-check gate (§17.5) over the published tree: zero misses
    27	  on marks and references, every fragment checked, no anchor trusted;
    28	  site-external references exempt and counted (D50).  The report's two
    29	  standing counters — stripped input-dangling references and exempted
    30	  site-external references — are the alarm every future data update is
    31	  checked by.
    32	* **patch** — on the machine with the turbopuffer key: one `patch_rows` run
    33	  writing `source_link` onto every row of the live namespace (§17.6, D49
    34	  ruling 3).  turbopuffer ignores a patch to an id that does not exist, and
    35	  the run counts the namespace before and after to prove no row was created.
    36	
    37	The artefact carries the recipe, not the string (Q4, 2026-08-23): per-record
    38	`(document id, file index, line)` triples ride beside the file→page map, and
    39	`source_links` composes each finished href at use time — one function, so a
    40	row's link can never disagree with the map it came from.  `needed_lines` is
    41	likewise derived from the same triples, so the marks the publisher injects and
    42	the lines the links point at are the same set by construction.

   120	def _canonical(body: dict) -> str:
   121	    return json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
   122	                      ensure_ascii=False)

   125	def write_artefact(path: str, body: dict) -> str:
   126	    """Writes `{"content_hash": …, "body": …}` and returns the hash.  Both the
   127	    scan output and the map artefact use this envelope — one shape for
   128	    anything that ships between machines (§17.1)."""
   129	    digest = hashlib.sha256(_canonical(body).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
   130	    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   131	        json.dump({"content_hash": digest, "body": body}, f,
   132	                  ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
   133	    return digest

   136	def load_artefact(path: str, kind: str, fmt: int) -> 'tuple[dict, str]':
   137	    """`(body, content hash)`, refused unless the hash still holds and the
   138	    body is the expected kind and format — the "one versioned artefact"
   139	    clause of §17.1, applied at every read."""
   140	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
   141	        stored = json.load(f)
   142	    body = stored.get("body")
   143	    digest = hashlib.sha256(_canonical(body).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
   144	    if digest != stored.get("content_hash"):
   145	        raise SourcePagesError(
   146	            f"{path} does not match its own content hash — a truncated copy or "
   147	            f"a hand edit; re-ship it from the machine that built it")
   148	    if body.get("kind") != kind or body.get("format") != fmt:
   149	        raise SourcePagesError(
   150	            f"{path} is kind {body.get('kind')!r} format {body.get('format')!r}; "
   151	            f"this step reads kind {kind!r} format {fmt}")
   152	    if kind == "map":
   153	        _validate_map_body(path, body)
   154	    return body, digest

   162	def _validate_map_body(path: str, body: dict) -> None:
   163	    """The structural facts the composer relies on, enforced at load rather
   164	    than remembered: every field present, `file_page_map` and `residue`
   165	    partition `files`, and every record's file index is in range."""
   166	    missing = [f for f in _MAP_FIELDS if f not in body]
   167	    if missing:
   168	        raise SourcePagesError(f"{path}: map body lacks {missing}")
   169	    files = body["files"]
   170	    mapped, residue = set(body["file_page_map"]), set(body["residue"])
   171	    if set(files) != mapped | residue or mapped & residue:
   172	        raise SourcePagesError(
   173	            f"{path}: file_page_map and residue do not partition files")
   174	    n = len(files)
   175	    if any(not (-1 <= fi < n) for _id, fi, _line in body["records"]):
   176	        raise SourcePagesError(f"{path}: a record's file index is out of range")

   179	def source_links(body: dict) -> 'dict[str, str]':
   180	    """Every record's finished link (D49 ruling 2), composed from the
   181	    artefact's own map: `page#L<line>` for a mapped position, the empty
   182	    string — D42's absent form — for no position and for residue alike.  THE
   183	    one place a source link is built (Q4), so the string a row carries can
   184	    never disagree with the map it came from."""
   185	    fpm = body["file_page_map"]
   186	    pages = [fpm.get(f) for f in body["files"]]
   187	    links = {doc_id: (f"{pages[fi]}#{line_fragment(line)}"
   188	                      if fi >= 0 and pages[fi] else "")
   189	             for doc_id, fi, line in body["records"]}
   190	    if len(links) != len(body["records"]):
   191	        raise SourcePagesError(
   192	            f"{len(body['records'])} record(s) yielded {len(links)} link(s) — "
   193	            f"duplicate document ids")

   197	def needed_lines_by_page(body: dict) -> 'dict[str, list[int]]':
   198	    """The marks each published page needs, derived from the same triples the
   199	    links compose from (Q4) — the injected marks and the lines the links point
   200	    at are the same set by construction, not by a checked coincidence."""
   201	    fpm = body["file_page_map"]
   202	    pages = [fpm.get(f) for f in body["files"]]
   203	    needed: 'dict[str, set[int]]' = {}
   204	    for _doc_id, fi, line in body["records"]:
   205	        if fi >= 0 and pages[fi]:
   206	            needed.setdefault(pages[fi], set()).add(line)

   214	def run_scan(*, isabelle_home: str, afp_dir: str, out: str) -> None:
   215	    """The corpus scan: the per-record position triples and the
   216	    declaring-theory evidence, from exactly the record set the export
   217	    publishes.
   218	
   219	    Every published document id rides in `records` — a record with no linkable
   220	    position with file index -1, because the patch writes `source_link` onto
   221	    every row (D49 ruling 3), empty string included.  `records` is sorted by
   222	    document id, so the scan's content hash does not depend on the store's
   223	    enumeration order.  `declaring_theory_hashes` feeds §17.3's cross-check:
   224	    per `.thy` position file, the declaring-theory hashes of the
   225	    name-addressed records positioned there — an XOR-prefixed key's 16-byte
   226	    prefix is a pseudo-theory (D13) and never enters."""
   227	    from Isabelle_RPC_Host.universal_key import is_xor_prefixed_key
   228	    from .site_export import declared_sessions, document_id, iter_shippable, theory_registry
   229	
   230	    sessions = declared_sessions(isabelle_home, afp_dir)
   231	    _log(f"{len(sessions)} declared session(s) in scope (D24)")
   232	    registry = theory_registry()
   233	    _log(f"{len(registry)} theory-hash registry entr(ies)")
   234	
   235	    counts: 'dict[str, int]' = dict.fromkeys(
   236	        ("records", "undecodable", "wip", "experience", "out of scope"), 0)
   237	    file_index: 'dict[str, int]' = {}
   238	    declaring: 'dict[str, set[str]]' = {}
   239	    records: 'list[list]' = []
   240	    pairs: 'set[tuple[int, int]]' = set()
   241	    for key, rec, _theories in iter_shippable(sessions, registry, counts):
   242	        pos = rec.position
   243	        if pos and linkable(pos[0]):
   244	            file, line = pos[0], pos[1]
   245	            fi = file_index.setdefault(file, len(file_index))
   246	            pairs.add((fi, line))
   247	            if file.endswith(".thy") and not is_xor_prefixed_key(key):
   248	                declaring.setdefault(file, set()).add(key[:16].hex())
   249	            records.append([document_id(key), fi, line])
   250	        else:
   251	            records.append([document_id(key), -1, 0])
   252	    records.sort()
   253	
   254	    body = {
   255	        "kind": "scan",
   256	        "format": SCAN_FORMAT,
   257	        "files": list(file_index),      # insertion-ordered: index i is files[i]
   258	        "declaring_theory_hashes": {f: sorted(h) for f, h in declaring.items()},
   259	        "records": records,
   260	    }
   261	    digest = write_artefact(out, body)
   262	    for what, n in counts.items():
   263	        _log(f"  {what:<14} {n}")
   264	    _log(f"wrote {out} (content hash {digest[:12]}): {len(records)} record(s), "
   265	         f"{len(file_index)} linkable position file(s), {len(pairs)} needed "
   266	         f"(file, line) pair(s)")

   273	class RenderedTree:
   274	    """One walk's worth of classification.  `raw_theory` holds each depth-3
   275	    theory page as `(session dir, stem, tree-relative path)` — the long name
   276	    is derived from it later, against the registry (D52).  `dropped` counts
   277	    what §17.2 declares out; anything unclassifiable is dropped and named in
   278	    the report rather than refused (D49 ruling 4)."""
   279	
   280	    def __init__(self) -> None:
   281	        self.raw_theory: 'list[tuple[str, str, str]]' = []
   282	        self.aux_copies: 'dict[str, list[str]]' = {}  # symbolic position -> paths
   283	        self.css_copies: 'list[str]' = []
   284	        self.fonts: 'list[str]' = []
   285	        self.dropped: 'dict[str, int]' = {}
   286	        self.unclassified: 'list[str]' = []
   287	        # EVERY file the walk saw, kept and dropped alike, with its size (Q3):
   288	        # the sealed set D51's dangling decision reads instead of the live
   289	        # filesystem, and what the tree fingerprint derives from.
   290	        self.inventory: 'dict[str, int]' = {}
   291	
   292	    def _drop(self, what: str) -> None:
   293	        self.dropped[what] = self.dropped.get(what, 0) + 1

   296	def classify_rendered_tree(root: str) -> RenderedTree:
   297	    tree = RenderedTree()
   298	    for dirpath, _dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
   299	        rel_dir = os.path.relpath(dirpath, root)
   300	        for name in filenames:
   301	            rel = name if rel_dir == "." else f"{rel_dir}/{name}".replace(os.sep, "/")
   302	            tree.inventory[rel] = os.path.getsize(os.path.join(dirpath, name))
   303	            parts = rel.split("/")
   304	            if ".browser_info" in parts:
   305	                tree._drop(".browser_info bookkeeping")
   306	            elif name == "isabelle.css":
   307	                tree.css_copies.append(rel)
   308	            elif name == "index.html" and len(parts) <= 3:
   309	                tree._drop("renderer index page")      # root, chapter or session
   310	            elif parts[0] == "fonts" and len(parts) == 2:
   311	                tree.fonts.append(rel)
   312	            elif name == "session_graph.pdf":
   313	                tree._drop("session graph")
   314	            elif name == "isabelle.gif":
   315	                tree._drop("isabelle.gif")
   316	            elif len(parts) == 3 and name.endswith(".html"):
   317	                tree.raw_theory.append((parts[1], name[:-len(".html")], rel))
   318	            elif len(parts) >= 4 and (sym := aux_symbolic("/".join(parts[2:]))):
   319	                tree.aux_copies.setdefault(sym, []).append(rel)
   320	            else:
   321	                tree._drop("unclassified")
   322	                tree.unclassified.append(rel)
   323	    for copies in tree.aux_copies.values():
   324	        copies.sort()
   325	    tree.raw_theory.sort(key=lambda t: t[2])
   326	    return tree

   329	def derive_theory_pages(raw_theory: 'list[tuple[str, str, str]]',
   330	                        registry_names: 'set[str]',
   331	                        ) -> 'tuple[dict[str, str], list[str]]':
   332	    """D52's verified derivation: `(long name → tree-relative path, dropped
   333	    page paths)`.
   334	
   335	    A stem containing `.` IS the long name — a theorem, not a heuristic:
   336	    `Long_Name` makes a dot in a base name impossible, so a dotted stem proves
   337	    foreign-session presentation and `print_short` = the full name.  A dotless
   338	    stem resolves to `<session dir>.<stem>` when the registry holds that name,
   339	    else to the bare stem (the global theories); a page resolving to neither
   340	    is dropped and reported (measured: the four Pure bootstrap/example pages,
   341	    zero entity ids, nothing pointing at them)."""
   342	    pages: 'dict[str, str]' = {}
   343	    dropped: 'list[str]' = []
   344	    for session_dir, stem, rel in raw_theory:
   345	        if "." in stem:
   346	            long_name = stem
   347	        elif f"{session_dir}.{stem}" in registry_names:
   348	            long_name = f"{session_dir}.{stem}"
   349	        elif stem in registry_names:
   350	            long_name = stem
   351	        else:
   352	            dropped.append(rel)
   353	            continue
   354	        if long_name in pages:
   355	            raise SourcePagesError(
   356	                f"pages {pages[long_name]} and {rel} both derive the long name "
   357	                f"{long_name!r} — long names are unique, so the derivation or "
   358	                f"the tree is broken")
   359	        pages[long_name] = rel
   360	    return pages, dropped

   363	def page_for_name(name: str, theory_pages: 'dict[str, str]') -> 'str | None':
   364	    """The published page key serving theory `name` (§17.3's page choice):
   365	    the name itself; for a bare name, the session-qualified twin page wins
   366	    when both exist; for an `X.X` name with no page, the bare page `X` — the
   367	    global-theory presentation of the same theory (D52's amendment,
   368	    `HOL-CSP.HOL-CSP` being the one such name today)."""
   369	    if "." not in name and f"{name}.{name}" in theory_pages:
   370	        return f"{name}.{name}"
   371	    if name in theory_pages:
   372	        return name
   373	    base = name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
   374	    if name == f"{base}.{base}" and base in theory_pages:
   375	        return base
   376	    return None

   379	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   380	# §17.3 — the file→page map: one lookup over data/theories.json (D53)
   381	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   382	
   383	def invert_theories(theories: dict) -> 'tuple[dict[str, str], dict[str, str]]':
   384	    """`(path → long name, the two tree prefixes)` from `data/theories.json`.
   385	
   386	    Folds the `(global)`-alias twins first — `X.X` beside `X` with the same
   387	    path is the session-qualified alias of a global theory (the same fold
   388	    `data/isabelle.py` applies at load; stated twice because this module must
   389	    run from a bare checkout on cslh19).  The inversion must be injective:
   390	    two long names on one path after the fold is a hard error, not a pick.
   391	
   392	    The prefixes are detected from the table itself: every path sits under
   393	    exactly one of two roots — the AFP snapshot (the one containing `/thys/`)
   394	    and the distribution."""
   395	    aliases = set()
   396	    for a in theories:
   397	        if "." in a:
   398	            b = a.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
   399	            if (a == f"{b}.{b}" and b in theories
   400	                    and theories[b]["path"] == theories[a]["path"]):
   401	                aliases.add(a)
   402	    inverted: 'dict[str, str]' = {}
   403	    for name, info in theories.items():
   404	        if name in aliases:
   405	            continue
   406	        path = info["path"]
   407	        if path in inverted:
   408	            raise SourcePagesError(
   409	                f"theories.json maps both {inverted[path]!r} and {name!r} to "
   410	                f"{path!r} — the inversion must be injective")
   411	        inverted[path] = name
   412	
   413	    # The AFP root is the prefix up to `/thys/` (no distribution path contains
   414	    # that segment — measured); the distribution root is the literal common
   415	    # string prefix of everything else, cut at its last `/` — NOT
   416	    # `posixpath.commonpath`, which normalises the leading `./` away.  The
   417	    # check below is the invariant `normalize_position` actually needs, not a
   418	    # proxy: every path must start with exactly one of the two prefixes.
   419	    # (Distribution components live under `contrib/`, not `src/` — the four
   420	    # Naproche theories are the measured case a `/src/` split would break.)
   421	    afp_set = {p[:p.index("/thys/") + len("/thys/")]
   422	               for p in inverted if "/thys/" in p}
   423	    if len(afp_set) != 1:
   424	        raise SourcePagesError(
   425	            f"theories.json's AFP paths sit under {len(afp_set)} roots: "
   426	            f"{sorted(afp_set)}")
   427	    afp = afp_set.pop()
   428	    home_paths = [p for p in inverted if "/thys/" not in p]
   429	    common = os.path.commonprefix(home_paths)
   430	    home = common[:common.rindex("/") + 1] if "/" in common else ""
   431	    bad = [p for p in inverted
   432	           if p.startswith(afp) == p.startswith(home) or not (
   433	               p.startswith(afp) or p.startswith(home))]
   434	    if not home or bad:
   435	        raise SourcePagesError(
   436	            f"theories.json paths do not partition under two roots "
   437	            f"(afp={afp!r}, home={home!r}); offending: {bad[:5]}")
   438	    return inverted, {"$AFP/": afp, "~~/": home}

   441	def normalize_position(file: str, prefixes: 'dict[str, str]') -> str:
   442	    """A symbolic position as `theories.json` spells the same file."""
   443	    for sym, real in prefixes.items():
   444	        if file.startswith(sym):
   445	            return real + file[len(sym):]
   446	    raise SourcePagesError(f"{file!r} is not a symbolic position")

   449	def build_file_page_map(scan: dict, inverted: 'dict[str, str]',
   450	                        prefixes: 'dict[str, str]',
   451	                        registry_by_hash: 'dict[str, str]',
   452	                        theory_pages: 'dict[str, str]', aux_copies: 'dict[str, list[str]]',
   453	                        ) -> 'tuple[dict[str, str], dict[str, str], list[str]]':
   454	    """D53's resolver, `(file → published page, residue)`.  For a `.thy` file
   455	    the answer is one table lookup, and each of the three staleness gates is a
   456	    hard error, not residue: a position file the table misses (coverage is
   457	    100 % by construction), a table name contradicting the file's
   458	    declaring-hash evidence (zero-conflict cross-check), a resolved name
   459	    without a page.  Residue exists only for auxiliary files with no rendered
   460	    copy."""
   461	    declaring = scan["declaring_theory_hashes"]
   462	    file_page_map: 'dict[str, str]' = {}
   463	    residue: 'dict[str, str]' = {}
   464	    no_evidence: 'list[str]' = []
   465	    for file in scan["files"]:
   466	        if file.endswith(".thy"):
   467	            name = inverted.get(normalize_position(file, prefixes))
   468	            if name is None:
   469	                raise SourcePagesError(
   470	                    f"{file} is not in theories.json — the table is stale for "
   471	                    f"this corpus generation; regenerate it (D53)")
   472	            hashes = declaring.get(file)
   473	            if hashes:
   474	                named = {registry_by_hash[h] for h in hashes if h in registry_by_hash}
   475	                # No resolvable hash is absence of evidence, not contradicting
   476	                # evidence — this registry may simply not know the file.
   477	                if not named:
   478	                    no_evidence.append(file)
   479	                elif name not in named:
   480	                    raise SourcePagesError(
   481	                        f"{file}: theories.json says {name!r} but the file's "
   482	                        f"name-addressed records name {sorted(named)} — the two "
   483	                        f"evidence chains disagree (D53's cross-check)")
   484	            page = page_for_name(name, theory_pages)
   485	            if page is None:
   486	                raise SourcePagesError(
   487	                    f"{file} resolves to {name!r}, which derives no published "
   488	                    f"page — the table and the rendered tree are not the same "
   489	                    f"generation (D53)")
   490	            file_page_map[file] = f"{SITE_PREFIX}{page}.html"
   491	        elif file in aux_copies:
   492	            file_page_map[file] = aux_page(file)
   493	        else:
   494	            residue[file] = "no rendered auxiliary copy"
   495	
   496	    page_of: 'dict[str, str]' = {}
   497	    for file, page in file_page_map.items():
   498	        if page in page_of:
   499	            raise SourcePagesError(
   500	                f"{page_of[page]} and {file} both map to {page} — two files "
   501	                f"cannot share one page's line marks")
   502	        page_of[page] = file
   503	    return file_page_map, residue, no_evidence

   506	def tree_fingerprint(inventory: 'dict[str, int]') -> str:
   507	    """sha256 over `rel\\0size` of the whole sealed inventory, sorted (Q3) —
   508	    a value derived from the inventory, never a second source of truth."""
   509	    h = hashlib.sha256()
   510	    for rel in sorted(inventory):
   511	        h.update(f"{rel}\0{inventory[rel]}\n".encode("utf-8"))
   512	    return h.hexdigest()

   515	# The two generated files claim their published paths before any relocated
   516	# file can (the collision guard pre-seeds them).
   517	GENERATED_PAGES = (f"{SITE_PREFIX}index.html", f"{SITE_PREFIX}isabelle.css")

   519	
   520	def build_relocation(classification: dict) -> 'dict[str, str]':
   521	    """THE map from every kept rendered file to its published path — built
   522	    once from the classification and used for the rewrite, the walk and the
   523	    fingerprint alike, so the set publish transforms and the set the seal
   524	    covers cannot diverge.  Collisions are checked per class: theory pages
   525	    and fonts are one-to-one, the auxiliary copies and the stylesheet copies
   526	    are many-to-one **by construction** (keyed by symbolic path / collapsing
   527	    to the one generated stylesheet), and the generated pages' paths are
   528	    pre-claimed."""
   529	    relocation: 'dict[str, str]' = {}
   530	    claimed: 'dict[str, str]' = {page: "<generated>" for page in GENERATED_PAGES}
   531	
   532	    def claim(rel: str, page: str) -> None:
   533	        if page in claimed:
   534	            raise SourcePagesError(
   535	                f"{claimed[page]} and {rel} both publish to {page}")
   536	        claimed[page] = rel
   537	        relocation[rel] = page
   538	
   539	    for name, rel in classification["theory_pages"].items():
   540	        claim(rel, f"{SITE_PREFIX}{name}.html")
   541	    for sym, rels in classification["aux_pages"].items():
   542	        page = aux_page(sym)
   543	        claim(rels[0], page)
   544	        for rel in rels[1:]:
   545	            relocation[rel] = page        # many-to-one by construction
   546	    for rel in classification["fonts"]:
   547	        claim(rel, f"{SITE_PREFIX}fonts/{rel.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]}")
   548	    for rel in classification["css"]:
   549	        relocation[rel] = f"{SITE_PREFIX}isabelle.css"   # collapses by design
   550	    return relocation

   553	def run_map(*, scan_path: str, rendered: str, theories_path: str, out: str,
   554	            repo_root: 'str | None' = None) -> None:
   555	    """Builds the classification, the file→page map and the per-file source
   556	    line counts, and seals them — with the scan's triples, the table's and
   557	    the registry's identity, and the whole tree inventory — into the
   558	    artefact.  Runs on the host that holds the rendered tree, the registry
   559	    and the two source trees (the pipeline is host-generic: every input is a
   560	    path, and the seals below are what make the artefact trustworthy
   561	    wherever it was built)."""

   672	def classify_reference(ref: str, page_dir: str):
   673	    """One reading of a reference value for the stripper, the rewriter and
   674	    the gate alike: `("external", None)` (D50), `("samepage", fragment)`, or
   675	    `("internal", (rendered-tree-relative target, fragment))` — resolved
   676	    against the page's rendered location."""
   677	    if is_external(ref):
   678	        return "external", None
   679	    target, _, fragment = ref.partition("#")
   680	    if not target:
   681	        return "samepage", fragment
   682	    resolved = posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(page_dir, target))
   683	    return "internal", (resolved, fragment)

   686	def assert_page_structure(page: str, page_rel: str) -> None:
   687	    """The structural facts §17.4 asserts per page — every page, not only the
   688	    marked ones, because "no newline inside a tag" is what licenses the tag
   689	    regex the reference rewrite runs on everywhere: exactly one
   690	    `<pre class="source">`, no newline inside any tag, and no pre-existing
   691	    `id="L<digits>"` the injected marks could collide with."""

   694	            f"{page_rel} has {page.count(_PRE_OPEN)} '{_PRE_OPEN}' elements, "

   704	class RefCounters:
   705	    """The report's standing alarm (D50/D51): exempted site-external
   706	    references, and stripped input-dangling anchors with their names."""
   707	
   708	    def __init__(self) -> None:
   709	        self.external = 0
   710	        self.stripped: 'list[tuple[str, str]]' = []   # (page rel, target)

   713	def strip_dangling_anchors(content: str, page_dir: str,
   714	                           relocation: 'dict[str, str]', page_rel: str,
   715	                           inventory: 'set[str]', counters: RefCounters) -> str:
   716	    """D51: an `<a>` whose site-internal `href` target does not exist in the
   717	    rendered tree — by the artefact's **sealed inventory**, never the live
   718	    filesystem (Q3) — is input-dangling: the renderer emitted a link to a
   719	    page it never wrote.  The anchor is stripped, its text kept (the page
   720	    reads identically, those words just stop being clickable), one WARNING
   721	    per target with the strip count, and the alarm counter counts **anchors**
   722	    (a page linking one dead blob five times counts five).  A target that
   723	    exists in the rendered tree but is missing from the relocation map stays
   724	    for `rewrite_html_refs` to refuse (broken-by-us is never papered over),
   725	    and a dangling `src=` is not stripped — it too falls through to the
   726	    rewriter's hard error, since D51 rules anchors only."""
   727	    dangling: 'set[str]' = set()
   728	    for tag in _TAG.finditer(content):
   729	        for m in _REF_ATTR.finditer(tag.group(0)):
   730	            if m.group(1) != "href":
   731	                continue
   732	            kind, payload = classify_reference(m.group(2), page_dir)
   733	            if kind == "internal" and payload[0] not in relocation \
   734	                    and payload[0] not in inventory:
   735	                dangling.add(m.group(2))
   736	    for ref in sorted(dangling):
   737	        pattern = re.compile(
   738	            r'<a\b[^>]*href="' + re.escape(ref) + r'"[^>]*>((?:(?!</?a\b).)*?)</a>',
   739	            re.DOTALL)
   740	        content, n = pattern.subn(r"\1", content)
   741	        if n == 0:
   742	            raise SourcePagesError(
   743	                f"{page_rel}: the dangling reference {ref!r} sits in a shape "
   744	                f"the anchor-stripper cannot cut (nested or unclosed <a>)")
   745	        counters.stripped.extend([(page_rel, ref)] * n)
   746	        _log(f"WARNING: stripped {n} dangling anchor(s) to {ref!r} on "
   747	             f"{page_rel} — the rendered tree never wrote that target (D51)")
   748	    return content

   751	def rewrite_html_refs(content: str, page_dir: str,
   752	                      relocation: 'dict[str, str]', page_rel: str,
   753	                      counters: RefCounters) -> str:
   754	    """§17.4's reference rewrite for a page: a site-external reference (D50)
   755	    is emitted byte-identically — not split at `#`, not resolved, not looked
   756	    up — and counted; every other `href`/`src` is split from its fragment,
   757	    resolved against the page's rendered location, mapped, re-emitted absolute
   758	    under `/source/`, fragment re-attached unchanged.  A reference the map
   759	    cannot name is a hard error naming the page and the reference."""
   760	    def fix_ref(m: 're.Match') -> str:
   761	        attr, ref = m.group(1), m.group(2)
   762	        kind, payload = classify_reference(ref, page_dir)
   763	        if kind == "external":
   764	            counters.external += 1
   765	            return m.group(0)
   766	        if kind == "samepage":
   767	            return m.group(0)             # a same-page fragment does not move
   768	        resolved, fragment = payload
   769	        published = relocation.get(resolved)
   770	        if published is None:
   771	            raise SourcePagesError(
   772	                f"{page_rel} references {ref!r} ({resolved}), which maps to no "
   773	                f"published file")
   774	        suffix = f"#{fragment}" if fragment else ""
   775	        return f'{attr}="{published}{suffix}"'
   776	
   777	    return _TAG.sub(lambda tag: _REF_ATTR.sub(fix_ref, tag.group(0)), content)

   780	def rewrite_css_urls(content: str, css_dir: str,
   781	                     relocation: 'dict[str, str]', css_rel: str,
   782	                     counters: RefCounters) -> str:
   783	    """The same rewrite for a stylesheet's `url()` references — per file type,
   784	    not per HTML attribute (§17.4); D50's predicate applies here too, so there
   785	    is one rule and not one per file type."""
   786	    def fix_url(m: 're.Match') -> str:
   787	        kind, payload = classify_reference(m.group(1), css_dir)
   788	        if kind == "external":
   789	            counters.external += 1
   790	            return m.group(0)
   791	        resolved = payload[0] if kind == "internal" else css_rel

   802	def inject_line_marks(page: str, lines: 'list[int]', page_rel: str,
   803	                      source_line_count: 'int | None') -> str:
   804	    """§17.4's injection: the window is the content of the page's single
   805	    `<pre class="source">` element; split on newlines, piece *n* is line *n*,
   806	    and each needed line gets an `<a id="Ln"></a>` prefix.
   807	
   808	    `source_line_count` is the real source file's line count the map recorded
   809	    (B3): the window must show the same number of lines, ±1 for the EOF
   810	    trailing-newline convention — the one check that catches a file mapped to
   811	    a page showing some other file's source, and any line-fidelity drift."""
   812	    head, _, rest = page.partition(_PRE_OPEN)
   813	    window, close, tail = rest.partition(_PRE_CLOSE)
   814	    if not close or _PRE_CLOSE in tail:
   815	        raise SourcePagesError(
   816	            f"{page_rel} does not close its source element exactly once")
   817	    pieces = window.split("\n")
   818	    if source_line_count is not None and abs(len(pieces) - source_line_count) > 1:
   819	        raise SourcePagesError(
   820	            f"{page_rel} shows {len(pieces)} source line(s) but the mapped "
   821	            f"file has {source_line_count} — wrong page, or the line-fidelity "
   822	            f"assumption broke (§17.4)")
   823	    for n in sorted(lines):
   824	        if not 1 <= n <= len(pieces):
   825	            raise SourcePagesError(
   826	                f"{page_rel} shows {len(pieces)} source line(s) but line {n} "
   827	                f"is needed — the line-fidelity assumption broke (§17.4)")
   828	        pieces[n - 1] = line_mark(n) + pieces[n - 1]
   829	    return head + _PRE_OPEN + "\n".join(pieces) + close + tail

   840	def merge_aux_copies(sym: str, copies: 'list[tuple[str, str]]',
   841	                     ) -> 'tuple[str, str, bool]':
   842	    """D49 ruling 6 as amended 2026-08-23: one auxiliary page per symbolic
   843	    path, publishing the id-union of all copies so every fragment reference
   844	    keeps landing.  `(base copy's rel, merged content, whether copies
   845	    conflicted)` — the caller must rewrite the merged content in the BASE
   846	    copy's directory context, since its reference strings are the base's.
   847	
   848	    The amended tolerance — the invariant measured true on all 12 real
   849	    conflicts: copies must agree **line-for-line in text once the title and
   850	    heading are set aside** (tags erased, `<title>`/`<h1>` lines exempt).
   851	    That admits the three measured conflict shapes the old byte-level test
   852	    refused — differing title wording, an entity-anchor *element* present in
   853	    one copy only, and reference strings resolved through different sessions
   854	    — while still refusing any real content divergence.  The base copy is the
   855	    one whose title names the symbolic path (ties broken by sorted rendered
   856	    location); ids other copies carry on a line become empty anchors at the
   857	    front of the base's line — same line, same landing."""
   858	    def title_names_sym(content: str) -> bool:
   859	        m = re.search(r"<title>([^<]*)</title>", content)
   860	        return bool(m) and sym in m.group(1)
   861	
   862	    ordered = sorted(copies, key=lambda c: (not title_names_sym(c[1]), c[0]))
   863	    (base_rel, base), *rest = ordered
   864	    if all(content == base for _rel, content in rest):
   865	        return base_rel, base, False
   866	    base_lines = base.split("\n")
   867	    merged = list(base_lines)
   868	    for rel, content in rest:
   869	        lines = content.split("\n")
   870	        if len(lines) != len(merged):
   871	            raise SourcePagesError(
   872	                f"{rel} and {base_rel} render one file with different line "
   873	                f"counts — beyond D49 ruling 6's amended tolerance")
   874	        for i, other in enumerate(lines):
   875	            if other == base_lines[i]:
   876	                continue
   877	            if _TAG.sub("", other) != _TAG.sub("", base_lines[i]) and not (
   878	                    _TITLE_OR_H1.search(other) or _TITLE_OR_H1.search(base_lines[i])):
   879	                raise SourcePagesError(
   880	                    f"{rel} and {base_rel} differ in text at line {i + 1} — "
   881	                    f"beyond D49 ruling 6's amended tolerance")
   882	            extra = _ids_in_tags(other) - _ids_in_tags(merged[i])
   883	            if extra:
   884	                anchors = "".join(f'<a id="{x}"></a>' for x in sorted(extra))
   885	                merged[i] = anchors + merged[i]
   886	    return base_rel, "\n".join(merged), True

    96	    if data is not None:
    97	        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    98	    for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
    99	        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers, method=method)
   100	        try:
   101	            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300) as resp:

   104	        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# §8.1 step 6 and §8.2 — the asset, the component guard, the namespace name
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def committed_asset_path() -> str:
    """Where the previous export's asset is, which is also where the CI gate and the
    JavaScript port read theirs (§16.6).  One file, so the invariant that makes the
    comparison meaningful — the committed asset is the deployed asset — needs no
    second declaration to keep in step."""
    return os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
                        "site", "tokenizer", "asset.json")


def asset_differences(committed_text: str, asset: dict, digest: str) -> 'list[str]':
    """The three counts D46's guard compares, in words: the `ISABELLE_SYMBOLS` file
    list, the `tokenizer_rule` version and the digest.

    All three, not the digest alone: the digest catches a table change but says
    nothing about *what* changed, and the file list is the thing D46 names as the
    declaration.  The `tokenizer_rule` comparison is what sees a rule change at all —
    a rule that touches no table leaves the other two untouched."""
    committed = json.loads(committed_text)
    committed_digest = hashlib.sha256(committed_text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    changes = []
    if committed.get("symbol_files") != asset["symbol_files"]:
        changes.append("the symbol files changed:\n"
                       f"  committed {json.dumps(committed.get('symbol_files'))}\n"

# Turbopuffer Query API Parameters

**(1) `aggregate_by` parameter:**

Request shape: `"aggregate_by": {"label": ["Count"]}` or `{"label": ["Sum", "attribute_name"]}`

Response: Results appear in the `"aggregations"` key when no `group_by` is specified. Example response:
```json
{"aggregations": {"my_count": 42}}
```

Example for counting documents:
```python
result = ns.query(
    aggregate_by={'my_cool_count': ('Count',)},
    filters=('cool_score', 'Gt', 7),
)
print(result.aggregations['my_cool_count'])
```

**(2) Maximum `top_k`:**

"Maximum: 10,000"

**(3) `In` filter — maximum values:**

The documentation does not specify a maximum number of values allowed in an `In` filter list.

**(4) `include_attributes` — non-existent attributes:**

The documentation states: "Attributes that do not exist in the schema are silently ignored" only for `exclude_attributes`. For `include_attributes`, behavior for non-existent attributes is not explicitly specified in this content.

**(5) `rank_by` ["id","asc"] with filters guarantees all matching rows:**

The documentation does not guarantee this. It states: "Similar to SQL, the ordering of results is not guaranteed when multiple documents have the same attribute value."

# Extract: turbopuffer Write API Documentation

## (1) `patch_rows` Operation

**Semantics & Non-existent IDs:**
"Patches documents in a row-based format. Identical to `upsert_rows`, but instead of overwriting entire documents, only the specified keys are written."

Critically: "Any patches to IDs that don't already exist in the namespace will be ignored; patches will not create any missing documents."

**Idempotency:** Not explicitly addressed in the documentation.

**Vector Patching Limitation:** "Vector attributes currently cannot be patched. You currently need to retrieve and upsert the entire document."

---

## (2) `schema` Field Behavior

**Partial vs. Full Update:**
The documentation states: "The write does not need to include any documents, i.e. `{"schema": ...}` is supported, provided the namespace already exists."

It also notes: "The schema can be passed on writes to manually configure attribute types and indexing behavior... This can be done on every write, or only the first; there's no performance difference."

**Schema Merging:** When you send a schema with only some attributes, the system treats it additively: "If a new attribute is added, this attribute will default to null for any documents that existed before the attribute was added."

**Conflicting Changes:** "Changing the attribute type of an existing attribute is currently an error."

---

## (3) Request Size Limits & Max Rows

**Payload Size:** "Write requests can have a payload size of up to 512 MB."

**Rows Per Request:** No explicit maximum stated for general write requests. However, filter-based operations have limits: "5M documents for `delete_by_filter`" and "50k documents for `patch_by_filter`."

---

## (4) Rate Limits & HTTP Status Codes

**HTTP 429 & Backpressure:**
"Disables HTTP 429 backpressure on writes when unindexed data exceeds 2 GB or 1 million rows, whichever comes first."

The `disable_backpressure` parameter controls this behavior. No other rate-limit thresholds or specific HTTP codes documented.

**HTTP 202:** "turbopuffer will respond with HTTP status 202 to queries that depend on an index that is not yet built." (Schema changes context.)

---

## (5) `distance_metric` on Existing Namespaces

**Requirement:**
"The function used to calculate vector similarity... required unless copy_from_namespace or branch_from_namespace is set or the namespace has no vector columns."

For existing namespaces without vector columns, `distance_metric` is not required. For namespaces with vectors already defined, the documentation does not explicitly state whether you must re-specify it on subsequent writes.

Based on the search results, I found relevant information about the Turbopuffer `aggregate_by` parameter with the `Count` function and how it's used in the query API.

## Summary

You can aggregate attribute values across all documents in a namespace that match the query's filters using the aggregate_by parameter. 

The `Count` aggregation function is used to count documents. Count documents without returning rows, and use grouped aggregations to split the counts by attribute.

### Example Usage

Here's how to use `aggregate_by` with the `Count` function:

To count documents grouped by the color and size attributes, you can use: `aggregate_by={"count_by_color_and_size": ("Count",)}` with `group_by=["color", "size"]`

The results are returned in `result.aggregation_groups`, which contains grouped rows with the aggregation values.

For basic document counting without grouping, you can also use `aggregate_by={"count_by_category": ("Count",)}` with optional `group_by` parameters to count rows per category.

content.content:
multi-query *without* `rerank_by` returns the legs separately, each row with
  its own leg's `$dist` (the vector leg's being the cosine distance D40
  displays). So server-side fusion and D40's display cannot share one round
  trip; fusing client-side over the unfused legs gets both in one. **Which side
  fuses — and whether D40's displayed number survives — is before the user**
  (options tabled 2026-08-21); this bullet only records what the API does.
  Engineering notes that must not be relearned: the fused row cap is root-level
  `limit` (root-level `top_k` is *silently ignored*); a BM25 leg's `$dist` is a
  relevance (higher is better, returned descending); at most 16 legs per
  request, executed with snapshot isolation.
- ~~**Does the f16 conversion change the ranking?**~~ **Measured 2026-08-21,
  end to end on the real published vectors: no.** 20 query vectors (15 spread
  across the id space, 5 topic-picked via BM25), each compared live-top-100
  against exact f32 cosine over the same candidates: top-10 identical and
  top-1 identical on all 20 queries; 2 adjacent swaps in 99,000 ranked pairs,
  both at exact-distance gaps below 2e-6 (ties for any practical purpose);
  displayed `$dist` differs from exact f32 cosine by at most 9.78e-6 — f16
  mantissa quantisation, two orders below display precision. D31's analysis
  holds. (Scope: drift *within* the served candidates; recall is the previous
  bullet's measurement.)
- ~~**Does the approximate-nearest-neighbour search still return the best members of a
  narrow filtered set?**~~ **Measured 2026-08-21 against the real index: yes,
  perfectly.** The two narrowest `kind` values — `proof method` (832 rows) and
  `named theorem bundles` (951 rows), selectivity ~0.06% of 1,337,025 — were
  each queried with three semantically unrelated real query vectors at top_k 20
  and 100 (12 measurements): every one returned the full requested top_k with
  recall 1.000 and an ordering byte-identical to exact cosine over the whole
  filtered set, which is the behaviour of exhaustive scoring inside a mask this
  small. §6.6's guarantee holds; the design problem this bullet feared does not
  exist. Side yield, exact via the aggregate endpoint
  (`{"aggregate_by": {"n": ["Count","id"]}}` works): the corpus has exactly 11
  `kind` values — lemma 1,031,439; constant 176,008; introduction rule 58,947;
  elimination rule 28,311; case-split rule 10,193; locale 9,928; type 9,420;
  induction rule 9,091; typeclass 1,905; named theorem bundles 951; proof
  method 832 — summing to the namespace's row count with nothing left over.
- ~~**What are the two source-link URL templates?**~~ **Settled 2026-08-20 by
  D47: there is one template, not two, and it points at pages we render and host
  ourselves.** The investigation this bullet asked for was run first and is what
  killed the external-link answer it assumed: the public pages are static output
  of Isabelle's own HTML presentation with per-entity anchors but no line
  anchors, the AFP side is keyed by session (not entry directory, which 404s for
  20 multi-session entries), and — decisively — both public sites track the
  *current* release while the corpus is pinned, so the user rejected linking out
  and chose self-rendering from the cslh19 umbrella build databases. Findings,
  template, and the pre-upload link-check gate are all recorded in D47. The
  warning this bullet carried survives as D47's gate: a template that 404s is
  worse than the absent form the other cards already show.

### 16.9 What is still blocked, and by whom

**Nothing outside this plan is blocking anything, as of 2026-08-20.** Per §12.2 all
three prerequisites are done: the key repair (D33) on 2026-08-18, the theory-hash
registry (B) and the entity positions reaching the published snapshot (C) on
2026-08-20. The tokenizer freeze never waited on any of them — D33 used to describe
itself as a prerequisite of the whole of phase one, which contradicted this; it is a
prerequisite of steps 4 and 5.

**The site export is written, 2026-08-20**, and it carried step 2's asset emission
with it as expected: `Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/site_export.py`, reached as
`isabelle-semantics site-export`. §8.1 says step by step what it does and what each
gate measured; §12.2's step 4 says what stands between it and a production namespace.

## 17. The source-page upload pass — design, as ruled by D49 (2026-08-21)

This section is the authority on the one transformation that takes the rendered
tree to the published tree, on the source-link column that D49's ruling 2 adds
to every row, and on the link-check gate that refuses to let either ship
broken. Its first draft went through the adversarial review D49 records; every
figure below was measured against the real rendered tree and the real corpus
during that round.

Terms: **the rendered tree** is `~/.isabelle/Isabelle2025-2/browser_info/` on
cslh19 exactly as `isabelle build -n -o browser_info` left it — read-only
input, never modified. **The published tree** is the fresh output directory
whose contents go to the host verbatim; the pass creates it, writes it
completely, and atomically renames it into place — it never deletes or writes
into a directory it was handed, so a partially transformed tree is
unrepresentable, which is the entire idempotence story. **The file→page map**
is the pass's central artefact: for every source file some position names, the
published page that renders it. **The needed-lines table** is keyed by the
position file — not by theory: 85 % of positioned records have no declaring
theory at all (D13), 25 theories span up to 6 files, and one file carries
records of several theories, so the file is the only key that fits both
directions. (The review corrected this last count: the original "2 files"
counted `Restriction_Spaces-HOLCF.thy`, which is not a multi-theory file but
the twin phenomenon — one theory collected under two names — and its
duplicate side was deleted in the 2026-08-23 twin cleanup; the one genuine
case is `AutoCorres2/c-parser/CLocals.thy`, whose ML machinery mints entities
for 11 theories with positions in its own file.)

### 17.1 Inputs — host-generic, and single-host in practice

The pipeline binds to no machine (user-directed, 2026-08-23): every step's

repository's own Isabelle-side extractor (`tools/Theory_Info/Get_Thy_Info.thy`
→ `REPL_Aux.session_theory_infos`, a **static** scan of the component ROOTs
and theory headers — no heap is loaded), and it is the very input that drove
the umbrella builds, so it is same-generation with the heaps, the collection
and the rendered tree by construction.

1. **Normalise** the symbolic position (`$AFP/<x>` → the snapshot tree,
   `~~/<x>` → the distribution tree).
2. **Look up** the inverted table: path → the one long name (inversion is
   injective after the `(global)`-alias fold of the 2026-08-23 twin cleanup;
   measured zero multi-name paths over 11,524).
3. **Page**: the long name's published page by D52's derivation, with the
   two twin branches — both ruled 2026-08-23: a bare name `X` **prefers the
   session-qualified twin page `X.X`** when both pages exist (fires once on
   the real corpus), and an `X.X` name with no page of its own **falls back
   to the bare page `X`** (zero hits today — the alias fold pre-empts it —
   kept because its deadness is a property of this table generation, not a
   guarantee).  Ratified with them: the twin pages **both publish** and the
   index lists both (rendered cross-references point into each, so dropping
   either would break links); the line marks and every row link land on the
   qualified twin only.

every resolved name has a page, `.thy` residue is **zero** — including all
1,110 pure-lemma files that carry no name-addressed record. The former

input.description: Read §17.4-17.5 of the plan

content.content:
internal cross-references still use them); a reference the map cannot name is a hard error naming the page and the reference. **Except site-external references (D50)**: a reference whose value begins with a URI scheme (`^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.\-]*:`) or with `//` is emitted byte-identically — not split at `#`, not resolved, not looked up — and counted in the report; the same predicate, applied to the whole value before any fragment split, governs `href`/`src` and stylesheet `url()` alike, so there is one rule and not one per file type. Isabelle forbids `:` in every path element (`Path.illegal_char`), so no published page can be named in a way the predicate would mistake for a scheme. **And except input-dangling references (D51)**: a site-internal reference whose resolved target does not exist in the rendered tree — the input was already broken — has its `` element stripped, text kept, one WARNING per strip, every strip listed in the report. A target that exists in the rendered tree but is missing from the map remains a hard error: broken-by-us is never papered over. **Inject the line marks**: the window is the content of the page's single `
` element;
`split("\n")` it and prefix piece *n* with `` for each needed
line *n* — piece count *is* line count, so there is no line-1 or EOF edge.
Two structural facts guard every page, asserted per page because they are the
whole correctness argument: exactly one `
`, and no newline
inside any tag (both measured true across all 11,796 files). A needed line
with no piece to land on is a hard error — the line-fidelity assumption broke.
A page already containing `id="L"` is a hard error (measured: zero
today; the plain prefix `id="L` matches 555 innocent pages and must not be
the test). Finally the pass **generates** `/source/index.html` and
`/source/isabelle.css` from the map.

### 17.5 The link-check gate, on the published tree

- Every needed (file, line): the mapped page exists and carries `id="L"`
  — zero misses required.
- Every reference in every published file — `href`/`src` in HTML, `url()` in
  CSS — resolves inside the published tree, **fragments included**: a `#L`
  fragment must match an injected mark, an entity-anchor fragment must match
  an id on the target page. No fragment is trusted (D49 ruling 6 killed the
  trusted-anchors clause). A site-external reference — by §17.4's predicate
  (D50), applied to the whole value before any fragment split — is exempt
  from both checks: the gate verifies the published tree, and an external
  target is not the tree's to serve. It is counted and reported, never failed
  on; a root-absolute reference not under `/source/` remains a hard error,
  since the pass emits no such reference. **Fragments split by provenance
  (D54)**: one this pipeline composed or injected misses at zero tolerance;
  one inherited from the rendered pages is still checked but a miss is
  counted and reported — the renderer emits `offset_…` references it never
  anchors (106 today), and an inherited miss is a top-of-page landing, not
  a broken page.
- Every row's `source_link` from the namespace (sampled or dumped) is either
  empty or string-equal to a path the published tree serves with the named
  mark present — the end-to-end clause D49 ruling 2 bought.
- Reported, not failed: the unresolved-residue count (§17.3), the
  dropped-unreferenced count (§17.2), the exempted site-external count (D50,
  baseline 232), the stripped input-dangling count (D51, baseline 1), the
  inherited-fragment-miss count (D54, baseline 106), and the coverage
  figures — positioned 99.28 %, linked 99.28 % minus the residue.  The three
  D50/D51/D54 counters are the standing alarm for every future data update:
  read three numbers instead of re-auditing the tree.
