                           sample: int) -> int:

I have everything I need. Here is the review. --- # Reviewer B — turn 1: patch-readiness, regressions in the v3/D54 delta, real-data verification Everything below was checked against the actual code, the real artefact, the real rendered and published trees, or the turbopuffer docs. Nothing is inferred from the commit messages. 109/109 tests pass on my run. ## What I verified as sound (so the findings below are read in proportion) - **The artefact composes exactly 1,337,009 links** — 1,327,410 non-empty, 9,599 empty — equal to the row count the patch expects. Its self-hash is `31a4b060cfb1e56383326b1247f3b682c9f97f464b436e3a4fb804dad5bd4406`, which is byte-equal to `artefact_hash` in `~/isasearch-published/publish-report.json`. No duplicate document ids. - **20 randomly chosen composed links land byte-for-byte.** For each I resolved `/source/.html#L` into `~/isasearch-published` and searched for the literal ``. 20/20 present. - **The 16-row delta is fully explained and benign.** `art_NEW.json` (the pre-cleanup artefact, 2026-08-23 16:12) holds 1,337,025 ids — exactly the number the 2026-08-20 production export upserted. Diffed against the current artefact: **16 ids removed, 0 added, 0 surviving id changed its (file, line)**. All 16 sit in `$AFP/Restriction_Spaces-Examples/HOLCF/Restriction_Spaces-HOLCF.thy`. That is precisely the twin-duplicate cleanup §17.6 claims. - **`document_id` and `_hash128` are unchanged since commit a406986**, i.e. since before the production export. The ids the patch will send are minted by the same function that minted the live ids. - **Fragments survive the rewrite byte-for-byte.** 120 real theory pages, 180,920 fragment-bearing references: the multiset of fragment strings in the published page is identical to the rendered page on every one. `rewrite_html_refs` re-attaches `#{fragment}` verbatim and never splits an external reference at all. - **`patch_rows` + partial `schema` is documented-safe.** turbopuffer's write docs: patches to non-existent ids are ignored and never create rows; a schema on a write is *merged additively* — "if a new attribute is added, this attribute will default to null for any documents that existed before"; only changing an *existing* attribute's type is an error. Sending `{"source_link": {...}}` will therefore not disturb the live namespace's other 14 columns. `{"aggregate_by": {"n": ["Count","id"]}}` is recorded in the plan (line 4330) as measured working live. - **The merge rework is correct on the real data.** 22 multi-copy groups (20×2, one×3, one×5), 12 conflicted — matching the report. Every published aux page's id set is a superset of the union of its copies' ids; zero ids lost; the only surplus ids are injected line marks (`hypsubst.ML` gains exactly `L295,L298,L302`; `atomize_elim.ML` gains exactly `L22`). No group has copies of differing line counts. The suspected three-copy id-loss does not exist — the in-place `merged[i]` update is load-bearing in the *right* direction, since subtracting against the accumulated line is what stops a later copy re-injecting a duplicate anchor. - **Base selection**: in all 12 conflicts the winner's `` does contain the symbolic path. The title test genuinely *discriminated* in 3 (`$AFP/Case_Labeling/util.ML`, `smt_word.ML`, `word_lib.ML`); in the other 9 every copy's title named `sym` and the sorted-path tiebreak chose among equals — immaterial, since in the one case where two title-matching copies competed (`util.ML`) both are byte-identical (sha256 `7be2520331c21c9a…`). - **The strip-loses-an-id hazard is structurally absent, not merely absent by luck.** I checked the one anchor actually stripped: `<a href="AFP/PAPP_Impossibility/sat_data/papp_impossibility.grat.xz.html">` — no `id`. That page's published id set loses zero ids relative to the rendered one. More decisively, across a 300-page sample of the rendered tree there are **zero** anchors carrying both `id=` and `href=`: this renderer puts ids on `<span class="entity_def">`, never on a linking `<a>`, and the stripper's replacement keeps the inner content (including those spans) intact. - **The gate's namespace sample really does discriminate.** Stubbed against the real 1.3M-link set: correctly patched → 0 failures; sorted-prefix half-patched → 248 failures; the final checkpoint group (16,384 rows) unpatched → 6 failures. Only 8 of the 500 stratified sample ids have an empty composed link, so 492 sample points are discriminating. --- ## Ranked findings ### 1. MEDIUM-HIGH · `site_source_pages.py:1402-1411` (and `1339`) — the retry budget is too small for a 1.3M-row write, so the patch will probably need several manual restarts `patch()` calls `request(...)` with the default `attempts=6`. That gives a total backoff of 62 seconds (2+4+8+16+32) before it raises. Meanwhile the patch offers `PATCH_ROWS=4096 × BATCH_WORKERS=4 = 16,384` rows per round trip (I measured the real payload: mean 112 bytes/row, so ~458 KB per request), against a documented per-namespace ceiling of **10k writes/s**, and turbopuffer's default write backpressure engages "when unindexed data exceeds 2 GB **or 1 million rows**, whichever comes first". This run writes 1,337,009 rows — past that row threshold by design. **Failure scenario:** around 75-80 % through the run turbopuffer starts returning 429 while it indexes. 429 is in `_RETRY_STATUS`, so `request` backs off — but only for 62 s total. Indexing backpressure typically lasts longer. The batch raises `ExportError`, `list(pool.map(...))` propagates it, the checkpoint for that group is never written, and the run aborts. This is **not** data-corrupting: `patch_rows` is idempotent in its ids and the group is re-sent whole on resume. It just means the operator restarts, re-sends up to 16,384 rows, and hits the same wall again. **Fix direction:** give the patch its own retry budget — `request(..., attempts=12)` inside `patch()` yields ~5 minutes of backoff (2,4,8,16,32,60,60,60,60,60,60) — or expose `--attempts`. Optionally drop the patch's worker count so the offered rate stays under the ceiling. The export survived the same policy at 1.337M rows, but it did so at `BATCH_ROWS=256` spread over four hours; the patch is an order of magnitude denser per unit time. ### 2. MEDIUM-HIGH · process — §17.7's own acceptance criterion "the patch dry-run against a scratch namespace round-trips" is **unmet**, and two live behaviours have never been exercised The plan makes a scratch-namespace dry run an acceptance condition for this section. It has not been run. Two request shapes go to production having only ever met a Python stub: - **`"schema": {"source_link": …}` sent to a namespace whose stored schema has no such column.** The docs say this is an additive merge, so it should be fine — but four workers declare the new attribute in the same instant on the first group. If that races into a 4xx that is not in `_RETRY_STATUS`, the run aborts on its first group (recoverable, checkpoint untouched, but noisy). - **`include_attributes: ["source_link"]` in the gate's sample.** The query docs are explicit that *`exclude_attributes`* silently ignores unknown names, and say nothing about `include_attributes`. So a `gate --namespace` run *before* the patch may 400 rather than report empty links. That matters because a pre-patch gate is otherwise the cheapest way to prove the live id set matches the artefact. **Fix direction:** run the dry run. Copy ~2,000 real rows (no `source_link`) into a scratch namespace, patch it, gate it with `--namespace`, patch it again (idempotency), gate again. That single exercise settles the schema add, `include_attributes` on a fresh column, the 500-id `In` filter, concurrency, checkpoint/resume and the rerun-after-complete no-op, all at once — and it is the criterion the plan already demands. ### 3. MEDIUM · operational — the artefact and the default checkpoint live on volatile storage `/tmp` on this machine is a **24 GB tmpfs, already 21 % full**. Both the 70 MB `map-artefact.json` and the 67 MB `scan-v2.json` sit there. The publish report, the patch checkpoint and the gate all pin the artefact by content hash, so losing it mid-run means the resume is refused until the artefact is reproduced (re-running map on the same scan and tree is deterministic, so it *is* reproducible — but that is an hour you do not want to spend at that moment). The `--checkpoint` default is a bare relative filename, which lands in whatever the cwd is — in practice the shared repo working tree, which other agents are also using. **Fix direction:** copy the artefact to `~` before the patch (its self-hash check will confirm the copy), and pass an explicit `--checkpoint` under `~`. ### 4. MEDIUM · `site_source_pages.py:1360-1364, 1420-1425` — `_count()` can return `None`, which makes the "no row was created" proof vacuous `_count()` is annotated `-> int` but returns `got.get("aggregations", {}).get("rows")`, i.e. `None` whenever the response does not carry that key. The pre-check fails closed (`before != len(links)` → refusal), which is right. The **post**-check does not: if the operator has passed `--allow-count-mismatch` and both calls return `None`, then `after != before` is `False`, the run reports success, and the line prints "still holds None row(s)". The one guarantee the patch offers about not creating rows is then satisfied by two absences of evidence. **Fix direction:** raise in `_count()` when the aggregation is missing, rather than returning `None`. The gate's copy at line 1305 has the same shape and deserves the same treatment. ### 5. MEDIUM · `site_source_pages.py:1310-1312` — the stratified sample provably passes a namespace that is not fully patched, and raising `--sample` does not fix it `chosen = ids[::step][:sample]` with `step = len(ids)//sample` never reaches the end of the id space. With the real 1,337,009 ids and `--sample 500`, the last sampled index is 1,334,326, leaving **2,682 rows the gate never looks at**. I demonstrated it: stubbing a namespace where only those last 2,682 rows are unpatched, `_gate_namespace_sample` returns **0 failures** and the gate exits green. The counter-intuitive part: raising the sample can make it *worse*, because the blind tail is `N-1 - step*(sample-1)` and `step` is an integer division. | `--sample` | step | last sampled index | blind tail | |---|---|---|---| | 100 | 13370 | 1,323,630 | 13,378 | | 500 | 2674 | 1,334,326 | **2,682** | | 1000 | 1337 | 1,335,663 | 1,345 | | 5000 | 267 | 1,334,733 | 2,275 | | 10000 | 133 | 1,329,867 | **7,141** | Is it reachable today? Not by a crash: the final group is 9,905 rows (1,337,009 − 81×16,384), so a crash before the last checkpoint leaves 9,905 unpatched, of which 7,223 *are* sampled — I measured 6 failures for that case. But it *is* reachable via `--limit`, and it becomes reachable by a crash the moment `PATCH_ROWS` or `BATCH_WORKERS` changes. **Fix direction:** stratify by pinning both endpoints — `chosen = [ids[i * (len(ids)-1) // (sample-1)] for i in range(sample)]` — which gives a blind tail of zero at any sample size. One line. ### 6. MEDIUM · `site_source_pages.py:1400` vs `site_export.py:199` — the `source_link` column is declared twice, in two literals `run_patch` writes `schema = {"source_link": {"type": "string", "filterable": False}}` and `namespace_schema` independently writes the identical dict. They agree today; nothing makes them agree tomorrow. Given that turbopuffer treats *changing an existing attribute's type as an error*, a future edit to `namespace_schema` that the patch's literal does not follow would produce either a hard API error mid-patch or a column declared two different ways depending on which code path last touched the namespace. This is exactly the invariant-by-convention the project's review criterion rejects. **Fix direction:** have `run_patch` take the declaration from one place, e.g. `namespace_schema(0)["source_link"]`, or factor out a `SOURCE_LINK_SCHEMA` constant that both read. ### 7. LOW-MEDIUM · `site_source_pages.py:939` vs `955-966` — the docstring claims a per-read size verification the code does not perform `run_publish`'s docstring says "each file's size is verified again at the moment it is read". It is not. Lines 955-966 are a single bulk loop over `relocation` (12,108 entries, one `os.path.getsize` each — so no double-stat; the cost worry is unfounded) that runs *before* `os.makedirs(staging)`. The files are then opened and read later, with no size re-check. The commit message advertises this as the Q3 fix, so the claim is load-bearing in a way the code is not. In practice the exposure is a time-of-check/time-of-use window over a tree the spec calls read-only input, so the risk is near nil — but the sentence should describe what happens. **Fix direction:** either say "verified once, up front, against the sealed inventory", or actually compare `len(content.encode())`/`os.fstat` at read time. ### 8. LOW · `site_source_pages.py:877-881` — the title/h1 tolerance is a blanket pass over the whole line, and it fired 6 times on real data The guard reads `_TAG.sub("", other) != _TAG.sub("", base_lines[i]) and not (_TITLE_OR_H1.search(other) or _TITLE_OR_H1.search(base_lines[i]))`. So on any line where *either* side carries a `<title>` or `<h1>` tag, an arbitrary text divergence is accepted silently. Six real lines took that path, in 3 groups, all benign filename wording (e.g. base `File ‹$AFP/Case_Labeling/util.ML›` vs other `File ‹util.ML›`). Why it is safe today, and only today: across all 48 rendered copies `_TITLE_OR_H1` matches *only* lines 6 and 12, and those lines are exactly the standalone `<title>` and `<h1>` elements. No source line inside `<pre class="source">` can match, because source `<` is escaped as `<`. So the docstring's claim that the tolerance "still refus[es] any real content divergence" is true of this renderer's line layout, not of the check. It is the renderer keeping the hole shut, not the code. **Fix direction:** exempt only the *element's text*, not the whole line — strip `<title>…` and `

…

` content before comparing, then require the remainder to match. ### 9. LOW · `site_source_pages.py:882-885` — two latent merge defects, both measured absent Both are code-shape risks, not present breakage; I state them because turn 2 will otherwise re-find them. - **`merged[i] = anchors + merged[i]` prepends unconditionally**, including on line 6 — which is inside ``. A losing copy carrying an id on any head line would put `` inside ``, where a browser relocates or drops it and the fragment does not land. Measured: `extra_ids` is empty on lines 6 and 12 in all 12 conflicting groups, and no injection ever landed on the `
` open line.
- **Id uniqueness is line-scoped, not document-scoped.** `extra = _ids_in_tags(other) - _ids_in_tags(merged[i])` only subtracts against *that* line. If the base already carries id `X` elsewhere and a loser carries `X` on line *i*, `X` is injected and the merged document holds a duplicate id. Measured clean on all 12 groups and on every published multi-copy page.

### 10. LOW · `site_source_pages.py:1150-1151, 1224-1244` — D54 splits by *bucket of origin*, not by fragment provenance

`wanted` (the lenient bucket) is filled from **every** reference found in **every** published file — including the two files this pipeline generates. A fragment we composed and emitted into `/source/index.html` or `/source/isabelle.css` would be graded at inherited tolerance, i.e. merely reported. Today the invariant holds by measurement, not by construction: I checked the generated index — **10,596 references, 0 external, 0 carrying a fragment** — and the CSS emits only `url()` to fonts. So there is currently no composed reference with a fragment anywhere in `wanted`.

The related hazard the brief asked about — our own rewrite mangling a fragment, or the stripper deleting an id, producing a miss misclassified as inherited — I investigated and it is closed on both counts (see the verified-sound list: 180,920 fragments preserved exactly; zero `` anchors exist in the renderer's output).

**Fix direction (if wanted):** classify at insertion — when the gate reads a *generated* file, put its fragments into `wanted_own`. Three lines, and it turns a measured property into a structural one.

### 11. LOW · `site_source_pages.py:1254-1256` — "verified on N page(s)" is computed from one of the two buckets and undercounts by 109

The line prints `sum(1 for r in wanted.values() if any(r))`, which counts only pages carrying at least one non-empty *inherited* fragment, while `checked_fragments` counts inherited **and** composed. Measured on the real run: the gate printed **9,870**; the number of pages pass 2 actually visited is **9,979**; 9,810 pages carry composed fragments, of which **109 are own-only and invisible to the printed number** (169 are inherited-only). So the sentence "1,530,342 fragment(s) verified on 9,870 page(s)" attributes the whole fragment count to a denominator that excludes 109 of the pages it was verified on.

**Fix direction:** `len(set(wanted) | set(wanted_own))`, or better, count the pages pass 2 actually opened.

### 12. LOW · `site_source_pages.py:1223, 1245-1250` — the alarm's third number is unbounded in memory, hardcoded in prose, and compared to nothing

Three things in one place:

- `inherited_misses` is a cap-free list of `(rel, fragment)` tuples kept only to print its length and the first five. `fail()`, ten lines above, does the opposite and better: it keeps a counter and caps *logging* at 50. Two miss-reporting paths, two memory disciplines. The real-run ceiling is 1,043,996 inherited fragments (1,530,342 total minus 486,346 composed), so a pathological renderer regression would build a list of ~150 MB to print five lines.
- The log string hardcodes "baseline 106", so the code will keep claiming 106 forever after the baseline moves.
- **Of §17.5's three standing alarm numbers, the gate cross-checks exactly one.** The external count (232) is compared against the publish report and fails on disagreement. The D51 strip count (1) and the D54 inherited-miss count (106) are printed and compared to nothing — the "read three numbers instead of re-auditing the tree" discipline is, for two of the three, a human being remembering two integers. That is precisely an invariant by convention.

**Fix direction:** keep a counter plus a bounded sample; and put the three expected baselines somewhere the gate can compare them (a small expected-counters file, or fields in the artefact), so a drift fails or at least prints "baseline 106, got 143".

### 13. LOW · `site_source_pages.py:506-512, 622` — `tree_fingerprint` is a derived duplicate sealed beside its own source, with zero discriminating power

`tree_fingerprint` is a pure function of `inventory`, and `inventory` is itself in the artefact body. Nothing ever reads the field back — `_MAP_FIELDS` checks it is *present*, and no step compares it to anything (the Q3 rework replaced the old "publish recomputes the fingerprint" check with per-file size comparison against the inventory, which is strictly stronger). So it contributes exactly nothing to the artefact's content hash that `inventory` does not already contribute. Its own docstring says "a value derived from the inventory, never a second source of truth" — but storing it *is* the second copy.

This is not true of its two neighbours: `theories_sha256` and `registry_fingerprint` genuinely add discrimination, because `theories.json` and the registry are not in the body. Those earn their place.

**Fix direction:** drop the field, or drop `inventory` and keep the fingerprint (you cannot, since D51's dangling decision reads the inventory — so drop the fingerprint).

### 14. LOW · `site_source_pages.py:1090` — `os.rename` sits outside the `try`, so the atomic step is the one step with no cleanup

`except BaseException: shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True); raise` is correct and its Ctrl-C behaviour is what §17.4 promises ("removes its own staging", never a handed path). But the rename is *after* the block. If `out` came into existence between the initial existence check and the rename (another agent, a stale directory restored), the rename fails with `ENOTEMPTY`, staging is left on disk, and the error escapes as a bare `OSError` — which `run_from_args` does not catch, so the operator gets a traceback instead of the module's own message. Same for a Ctrl-C landing in that window.

**Fix direction:** move the rename inside the `try`.

### 15. LOW/pedantic · `site_source_pages.py:1026-1039` — the stylesheet's external count is "whichever copy the loop happened to finish on"

`css_counters = per_copy` reassigns the whole counter object each iteration and the code then uses the last one. It is correct — the copies are asserted to rewrite to one identical text, so any copy's count is the published count, and the comment says so. But it reaches the right answer by relying on a loop variable surviving the loop, when the right answer is available directly from the one surviving text: the index page four lines below already counts externals by re-scanning its own generated content. Doing the same to `rewritten_css.pop()` deletes `per_copy`, `css_counters`, and the reasoning that justifies them.

### 16. LOW/pedantic · `site_source_pages.py:1413-1417` — the checkpoint path is never validated before the first billed write

If `--checkpoint` names a path whose directory does not exist, the failure surfaces *after* the first group of 16,384 rows has already gone up, as an uncaught `OSError`. Recovery is safe (idempotent re-send from zero) but wasteful. Writing a `done: 0` checkpoint before the loop would validate the path at zero cost.

### 17. LOW/pedantic · `site_source_pages.py:733-734` — a reference to a *deliberately dropped* rendered file can only be a hard publish failure, never a graceful strip

`strip_dangling_anchors` strips only when the target is in neither `relocation` nor `inventory`. The 101 files that exist in the rendered tree but were dropped or left underived (34 renderer index pages, 30 session graphs, `isabelle.gif`, 34 `.browser_info` entries, 2 underived Pure pages) are *in* the inventory, so a reference to one falls through to `rewrite_html_refs`'s hard error. The real run is green because nothing references them — an invariant held by measurement. If a future Isabelle release starts emitting an "up to session index" link on theory pages, publish stops dead rather than degrading. Worth knowing; arguably the correct behaviour, since silently dropping a link the renderer meant is not obviously better.

### 18. LOW/pedantic · `site_source_pages.py:1311-1315` — `--sample 0` sends a degenerate query

`max(1, sample)` guards the division but `chosen` then becomes `[]`, and the code still issues a query with `top_k: 0` and `filters ["id","In",[]]`. `len(rows) < len(chosen)` is `0 < 0`, so it reports "0 row(s) compared, stratified" and passes. Only reachable via an explicit `--sample 0 --namespace`.

### 19. pedantic · `site_export.py:807-808` — continuation line misindented

`links_digest)` sits at column 46 where the opening paren puts it at 50. Cosmetic, but it is the one visible seam where the fix batch was applied in a hurry.

### 20. Note, not a defect · the patch is additive-only

`run_patch` iterates the artefact's ids. A row the namespace holds that the artefact does not name keeps whatever `source_link` it already had — stale or null — forever. The count precondition is the only thing standing between that and a silent inconsistency, and equal counts do not imply equal id sets (N added + N removed passes). Today this is fine: I proved the id sets differ by exactly the 16 deletions and nothing else. It is worth writing down because the next data generation will not have that proof handed to it.

---

None. Every finding above is either a code fix, a doc fix, or an operational precaution. I am not proposing to relax D49, D50, D51, D54 or §17.5's zero-miss requirement in any respect.

Here is my review. --- # Reviewer B — turn 1: patch-readiness, regression hunt, real-data verification Everything below was verified against the actual code, the real artefacts, or turbopuffer's own docs. 109 tests re-run green (0.51 s). The real gate re-run green (exit 0) on the published tree. --- ## Facts established (not findings — the evidentiary base) | What | Value | How | |---|---|---| | Artefact `31a4b060cfb1…` composes | **1,337,009** links (1,327,410 non-empty, 9,599 empty) | composed `source_links` over the real 70 MB artefact | | Publish report's `artefact_hash` | `31a4b060cfb1…` — matches | read | | Namespace as exported 2026-08-20 | **1,337,025** rows | plan §16.8/§17.6, live-measured | | Pre-cleanup artefact `art_NEW.json` (08-23 16:12) | 1,337,025 ids | loaded | | Delta to today's artefact | **16 removed, 0 added, 0 surviving id changed its (file,line)** | set diff | | The 16 | all `$AFP/Restriction_Spaces-Examples/HOLCF/Restriction_Spaces-HOLCF.thy` | printed | | `document_id` / `_hash128` | unchanged since `a406986`, i.e. before the production export | `git log -L` | | Mean patch row | 112 B; a 4096-row batch body ≈ **458 KB** | measured | | 20 random composed links | **20/20 land byte-for-byte** on `` in `~/isasearch-published` | verified | | Fragment byte-preservation | 320 real pages, **464,757 fragment-bearing references, zero fragment strings changed** | measured (mine: 120 pages/180,920; agent: 200 pages/283,837) | | Merge on real data | 22 multi-copy groups (sizes 2, 3, 5), **12 conflicted**, **0 ids lost** in any published aux page | re-ran `merge_aux_copies` over the real tree | **Turbopuffer docs settle two of the three feared unknowns, favourably:** - `patch_rows`: "patches to IDs that don't already exist … will be ignored; patches will not create any missing documents." Only named keys written. ✔ - `schema` on a write is **additive, not a replacement**: "If a new attribute is added, this attribute will default to null for any documents that existed before"; it "can be passed on every write … there's no performance difference"; only *changing an existing attribute's type* is an error. So sending `{"source_link": …}` on a namespace whose stored schema lacks the column **adds** it and does **not** drop the other 15 columns. The declared shape (`string`, `filterable: False`) is byte-identical to `namespace_schema`'s, so there is no type conflict either. ✔ --- ## Ranked findings ### 1. HIGH (operational) — the retry budget is far too small for a 1.3-million-row write `site_source_pages.py:1402-1411`. `patch()` calls `request(...)` with the default `attempts=6`, whose total backoff is **62 seconds** (2+4+8+16+32). turbopuffer's documented ceilings: **10k writes/s per namespace**, and default HTTP-429 write backpressure engaging once unindexed data exceeds **2 GB or 1 million rows**. This run writes **1,337,009 rows** at 4 concurrent × 4,096-row requests — up to 16,384 rows per round trip, ~458 KB per request. **Failure scenario:** somewhere past the 1M-row mark the service starts 429-ing while it indexes; 429 *is* in `_RETRY_STATUS`, so `request` backs off — but it gives up after 62 s and raises `ExportError`, aborting the run. Not corrupting (the checkpoint did not advance, `patch_rows` is idempotent), but it means repeated manual restarts, each re-sending up to 16,384 rows. **Fix:** give the patch its own budget — `request(..., attempts=12)` (~5 minutes of backoff) inside `patch()`, or an `--attempts` flag. Optionally halve the in-flight batch size for the patch. This is the single most likely thing to actually happen on the night. ### 2. HIGH (process) — §17.7's own acceptance criterion is unmet: "the patch dry-run against a scratch namespace round-trips" `SEMANTIC_SEARCH_SITE_PLAN.md:4623`. The plan lists this as a condition of acceptance and it has not been done. Three request shapes still go to production having never touched the real service: - `"schema": {"source_link": …}` **adding a column to a namespace that lacks it** — documented safe, never exercised; and four workers declare the new attribute simultaneously on the very first group. - `include_attributes: ["source_link"]` (`:1316`) against a namespace where the column may not exist yet — the query docs state that *`exclude_attributes`* silently ignores unknown names and say **nothing** about `include_attributes`. So a pre-patch `gate --namespace` may 400. - an `id In` filter carrying **500** values (`:1315`) — the docs document no maximum for `In`. (The fourth shape, `{"aggregate_by": {"rows": ["Count","id"]}}`, *is* proven: plan line 4330 records it working live against this very namespace.) **Fix:** copy ~2,000 real rows into a scratch namespace, patch it, gate it with `--namespace`, re-patch it, re-gate. That one exercise closes all three unknowns at once and matches the criterion already written into the plan. ### 3. MEDIUM — `_count()` can return `None`, and then the "no row was created" proof is vacuous `:1360-1364` and `:1420-1425`. `got.get("aggregations", {}).get("rows")` yields `None` if the response ever lacks that key; the annotation `-> int` is a lie. Pre-check fails closed (`before != len(links)` → hard error) — good. But **with `--allow-count-mismatch`, `before` and `after` can both be `None`, `after != before` is False, and the run prints "still holds None row(s)" and exits successfully.** The whole point of the before/after pair evaporates. **Fix:** raise in `_count()` when the value is not an `int`; keep the annotation honest. ### 4. MEDIUM — the gate's stratified sample provably passes a namespace whose tail is unpatched, and enlarging the sample does not help `:1310-1312`, `chosen = ids[::step][:sample]`. Demonstrated by simulation against the real 1.3M-link set: | namespace state | failures reported | |---|---| | correctly patched | 0 ✔ | | sorted-prefix half patched | 248 ✔ | | last checkpoint group (16,384 rows) unpatched | 6 ✔ | | **last 2,682 rows unpatched** | **0 ✘ — gate passes** | The sample's last id is `ids[2674 × 499] = ids[1,334,326]`, leaving **2,682 rows never sampled**. And the obvious mitigation backfires, because the blind tail is `N-1 − step·(sample−1)` with integer `step`: ``` sample= 100 → blind tail 13,378 sample= 1000 → blind tail 1,345 sample= 500 → blind tail 2,682 sample= 5000 → blind tail 2,275 sample=10000 → blind tail 7,141 (worse!) ``` Today's checkpoint granularity means a crash always leaves ≥ 9,905 rows unpatched (the final group), so the hole is not reachable by a crash *right now* — but it is reachable via `--limit`, and it becomes reachable the moment `PATCH_ROWS` or `BATCH_WORKERS` changes. **Fix (one line):** pin both endpoints — `chosen = [ids[i * (len(ids)-1) // (sample-1)] for i in range(sample)]` — which makes the blind tail exactly 0 at every sample size. ### 5. MEDIUM (elegance / invariant-by-convention) — the `source_link` column is declared twice `site_source_pages.py:1400` restates `{"source_link": {"type": "string", "filterable": False}}` which `site_export.namespace_schema` already declares at `site_export.py:199`. They agree today (I checked byte-for-byte). If someone ever makes the column filterable in `namespace_schema`, the patch's private literal silently disagrees — and per the docs a mismatched declaration of an existing attribute is an error, so you would discover it as an aborted production write. **Fix:** `schema = {"source_link": namespace_schema(1)["source_link"]}`, or factor the one declaration into a named constant both read. ### 6. MEDIUM-LOW — `run_publish`'s docstring claims a size check the code does not perform `:939` — "each file's size is verified again **at the moment it is read**". The code (`:955-966`) runs one bulk `os.path.getsize` loop over all 12,108 relocation entries **before** staging is even created, and never re-checks at read time (`:1004`, `:1012`, `:1030`, `:1045`). The commit message advertises this as the Q3 fix. To settle the brief's other suspicion: there is **no** double-`getsize` — each file is stat'd exactly once, and the loop's cost is negligible. **Fix:** either say what it does ("every relocated file's size is verified against the sealed inventory before any file is read") or actually verify at read time. ### 7. LOW — D49 ruling 6's stated base-selection rule decides only 3 of the 12 real conflicts `:858-862`. Re-running the merge on the real tree: - **3 conflicts** have a genuine title-based winner (`$AFP/Case_Labeling/util.ML`, `~~/src/HOL/Library/Tools/smt_word.ML`, `~~/…/word_lib.ML` — the losers' titles read `File ‹util.ML›`, `File ‹Tools/smt_word.ML›`, `File ‹Tools/word_lib.ML›`). - **9 conflicts** have **identical titles on both copies** (all nine `~~/src/Provers/*.ML` and `~~/src/Tools/*.ML` pages read `File ‹~~/src/Provers/blast.ML›` on both sides). `title_names_sym` is True for both, so the base is picked purely by the alphabetical tiebreak (`HOL/HOL/…` beats `Unsorted/AFP-DEP1-0/…`), and what actually differs is reference strings resolved through different sessions. The docstring presents the tiebreak as an afterthought when it is in fact the deciding rule for 75 % of real cases. Outcome is still correct (all references are rewritten to absolute `/source/` paths, ids unioned, gate green), but the stated invariant is not the operative one. **Verified clean alongside it:** 0 ids missing from any published aux page vs the union across copies; no group has a line-count spread; the ≥3-copy accumulation path is correct by construction (`merged[i]` is compared, so a third copy sees the second's additions) though no real group exercises it with non-empty ids. ### 8. LOW — the merge's title/h1 tolerance exemption is line-granular, not element-granular `:877-878`. `if _TAG.sub("", other) != _TAG.sub("", base_lines[i]) and not (_TITLE_OR_H1.search(other) or _TITLE_OR_H1.search(base_lines[i]))` — a line containing a `` or `<h1>` **anywhere** gets a blanket pass on *any* text divergence. Isabelle puts the title on its own line so this is harmless today, but the rule as written admits more than "the title and heading set aside". ### 9. LOW (latent) — D54 classifies by *which bucket the reference was collected into*, not by the fragment's provenance `:1147-1180`. Pass 1 puts **every** reference found anywhere in the published tree into the inherited bucket — including the two files this pipeline generates. The composed bucket is fed only from row links and needed marks. This is right today **by measurement, not by construction**: I confirmed the generated index emits 10,596 references, **0 external and 0 carrying a fragment**, and the generated stylesheet's `url()`s carry none either. If `generate_index` ever emitted a `#…` link, that composed fragment would be graded at inherited (report-only) tolerance. **Related hazard, investigated and found structurally dead:** `strip_dangling_anchors` (`:736-745`) replaces the whole `<a …>` element with its inner text, so an `<a id="X" href="dangling">` would take `X` with it and any reference to `X` would then miss *as "inherited"* though the pipeline destroyed it. A whole-tree grep finds **zero** files where any element other than `<span>` carries an `id=`, in either attribute order — the Isabelle presenter puts ids on `<span class="entity_def">` and hrefs on bare `<a>`, and the two never meet. The one anchor actually stripped in the real run is `<a href="AFP/PAPP_Impossibility/sat_data/papp_impossibility.grat.xz.html">` — no id — and that page's published id set is exactly `252 + 34 injected marks = 286`, nothing lost. ### 10. LOW (reporting) — "verified on N page(s)" undercounts by 109 pages `:1254-1256`. `checked_fragments` counts both buckets; the page count is `sum(1 for r in wanted.values() if any(r))`, which reads only the inherited bucket. Measured on the real run: the gate printed **9,870**, pass 2 actually visited and verified fragments on **9,979**; **109** pages carry composed fragments but no inherited one and are invisible to the counter (169 are the reverse). **Fix:** count once per page actually entered in the pass-2 loop, or `len({rel for rel, r in wanted.items() if any(r)} | set(wanted_own))`. ### 11. LOW (elegance) — `tree_fingerprint` is a derived duplicate sealed beside its own source `:506-512`, written at `:622`. Nothing ever compares it (`_MAP_FIELDS` only checks presence; publish verifies sizes against `inventory` directly). Its only residual purpose is to perturb the artefact's content hash — but it is a pure function of `inventory`, which is *already* in the body, so it contributes exactly zero discriminating power. Its own docstring says "a value derived from the inventory, never a second source of truth", and the field is precisely a second copy. (`theories_sha256` and `registry_fingerprint` are **not** in this category — those inputs are not in the body, so they genuinely add discrimination. Keep them.) ### 12. LOW (elegance) — the standing alarm is only one-third automated The plan calls the three counters "the standing alarm … read three numbers instead of re-auditing the tree". The gate cross-checks **only** the D50 external count against the report (`:1271-1275`). D51's strip count and D54's inherited-miss count are printed and compared to nothing — and `:1248` hard-codes `"baseline 106"` into a log message that will keep asserting 106 forever. That is exactly the invariant-by-convention this project's review criteria reject. **Fix:** put the three baselines somewhere the gate can read and compare (a small expected-counters file, or fields in the artefact), and fail — or at least warn loudly — when one moves. ### 13. LOW — `os.rename(staging, out)` sits outside the `try` `:1090`, after the `except BaseException` block at `:1087-1089`. If the rename raises — `out` created by someone else between the `:948-952` existence check and here, or an interrupt landing in that window — the staging directory is left on disk *and* the exception is a bare `OSError`, which `run_from_args`'s `except (SourcePagesError, ExportError)` does not catch, so the operator gets a traceback instead of a message. (The `BaseException` handler itself is fine: removing its own staging on Ctrl-C is exactly what §17.4 promises, and `rmtree` before `raise` preserves KeyboardInterrupt semantics.) ### 14. LOW — the checkpoint path is never validated before the first network write `:1413-1417`. If `--checkpoint` names a path in a non-existent directory, the failure surfaces only *after* the first group of 16,384 rows has already gone up, as an uncaught `OSError` with no checkpoint written. Harmless (idempotent re-run) but wasteful and ugly. **Fix:** write a `done: 0` checkpoint before entering the loop — it validates the path and costs nothing. ### 15. LOW — a reference to a *dropped* rendered file can only be a hard publish failure, never a graceful strip `:733-734`: `payload[0] not in relocation and payload[0] not in inventory`. The inventory is the *whole* tree (12,209 files) including the 99 deliberately dropped ones and the 2 underived Pure pages. A reference to any of them is present-in-inventory but absent-from-relocation, so it bypasses D51's strip and hits `rewrite_html_refs`'s hard error. Correct by design ("broken-by-us is never papered over") and empirically fine — the plan measured "zero entity ids, nothing pointing at them" — but it means adding one page to `underived` in a future generation aborts publish rather than degrading. ### 16. LOW/pedantic — `css_counters = per_copy` is last-copy-wins `:1026-1039`. The external count for the stylesheet is taken from whichever of the 335 rewrites ran last, relying on the identity assertion two lines below. The generated index, four lines further on, counts externals directly off the text it is about to write — the cleaner idiom. Doing the same for the surviving stylesheet would delete both `per_copy` and `css_counters`. ### 17. LOW/pedantic — assorted - `merged_conflicts += conflicted` (`:1015`) adds a `bool` to an `int`. - `--sample 0` with `--namespace` sends a degenerate query (`top_k: 0`, `In: []`) and then reports "0 row(s) compared, stratified" as a pass. `sample` is never validated `> 0`. - `site_export.py:807-808`: continuation line under-indented by 4 (`links_digest)` does not align with `checkpoint`) — a visible edit-under-pressure artefact in the fix batch. - `classify_reference`'s `partition("#")` cannot distinguish `"a.html#"` from `"a.html"`, so a trailing bare `#` would be dropped on rewrite. Cosmetic; none observed in 464,757 sampled fragment-bearing references. - The patch is additive-only: it has no way to *clear* a `source_link` on a live row the artefact no longer names. Today the artefact names every row (counts equal), so this is inert. ### Not findings — checked and clean `invert_theories`'s prefix detection on the real table (`$AFP/` → `./contrib/afp-2026-05-13/thys/`, `~~/` → `./contrib/Isabelle2025-2/`, mutually disjoint; and every degenerate case fails closed via the `bad` check, never silently wrong). The plan's `9,784` is the `.thy` position-file count (9,810 total = 9,784 `.thy` + 26 auxiliary) — not stale. The `if total:` guard makes positioned-coverage division-by-zero unreachable, as does the `if links else` guard in `run_map`. The promised-pages loop's 1,139 `aux_page(sym)` values and 13 font basenames are collision-free (arity enforced at publish by `build_relocation`'s `claim`). Report-in-staging-then-rename is sound and `artefact_hash` is stamped from `load_artefact`, so the tree↔artefact binding is real. --- # PATCH-READINESS VERDICT: **GO with amendments** The design is right: `patch_rows` semantics, additive schema merge, sorted-id ordering, group-granular checkpointing pinned to the artefact hash, before/after count proof, and a stratified post-check that I demonstrated *does* discriminate a half-patched namespace. Nothing I found can corrupt data. The amendments are about not wasting a night and not signing off on untested request shapes. ### Amendments required before the run 1. **Move the artefact off tmpfs.** `/tmp` here is a **24 GB tmpfs, already 21 % full** — the 70 MB artefact and 67 MB scan are memory-resident and evaporate on reboot. The checkpoint and the published report are both pinned to hash `31a4b060cfb1…`. Copy first; `load_artefact` self-verifies the hash on every read, so the copy proves itself. 2. **Raise the retry budget** (finding 1). Without it, expect the run to abort on 429 backpressure and need several manual resumes. 3. **Do the scratch-namespace dry run** (finding 2) — it is the plan's own acceptance criterion and it closes all three untested API shapes. 4. **Do not pass `--allow-count-mismatch`.** If the count comes back 1,337,025 rather than 1,337,009, the 16 twin-duplicate rows are still live in turbopuffer and must be deleted first, not patched around. They are exactly: ``` 13f30a15-34c3-ba0c-4256-f71b4b7cd248 192716eb-4ac4-3e9e-22b6-8d69f9372e6e 1d0e2605-84a4-5891-5233-ed36c32763b7 1fa9f7a6-5bab-cab1-cd28-f86fdf51cfdb 24c7a322-95f2-30a1-9420-82bd69fd8638 381a5f2f-c271-7f06-c21d-375007fca7b4 38d3853a-67f6-c002-21c5-daabfa58f46c 3c25d018-3702-f59b-6863-af3bba0dc14b 56fd3540-0035-8b5f-54a5-c31e187f8d94 a63c8d15-cfb5-bdde-2ab9-a20a6751fcd2 b66ecc85-0544-287b-0597-066151b2cd89 d818c61c-732b-80b5-8368-aa2736380373 e07094eb-42ab-90b1-1140-345bcc593bf6 e6405867-45d1-6f34-94de-0d42903c124f fd64ae24-bfcb-1be4-881f-fe4955ec5930 fe112424-4827-8c87-c40c-9528d0c34144 ``` (Nothing in this repository ever deleted them from turbopuffer — the only delete path is a whole-namespace `DELETE` at `site_export.py:603`. The plan asserts they were removed; the count query is the only local proof.) 5. **Fix the sample's blind tail** (finding 4) before relying on the post-check, or add the explicit last-id probe in step 3 of the post-checks below. ### The exact invocation ```bash # durable copies first cp /tmp/claude-1002/-home-qiyuan-Current-MLML/191c16f2-3fa2-4e2b-b337-d141aea09fc8/scratchpad/map-artefact.json ~/map-artefact.json cp /tmp/claude-1002/-home-qiyuan-Current-MLML/191c16f2-3fa2-4e2b-b337-d141aea09fc8/scratchpad/scan-v2.json ~/scan-v2.json source ~/Current/MLML/secret.sh && export TURBOPUFFER_API_KEY="$turbopuffer_DEV_KEY" source ~/Current/MLML/envir.sh cd ~/Current/MLML/contrib/Semantic_Embedding python -m Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding.site_source_pages patch \ --artefact ~/map-artefact.json \ --namespace isasearch-2025-2-afp-2026-05-13 \ --region aws-us-west-2 \ --checkpoint ~/source-link-patch.checkpoint.json \ 2>&1 | tee ~/source-link-patch.log ``` No `--limit`, no `--allow-count-mismatch`. The checkpoint deliberately lives outside the repository — this is a shared working tree. Optional one-batch smoke first: append `--limit 4096`, confirm the log's `before` count reads exactly `1337009`, then re-run without `--limit` — resume is exact and the checkpoint arithmetic is unit-tested (`test_a_resume_patches_only_the_remaining_ids`). Expected log shape: `isasearch-…: 1337009 row(s); artefact composes 1337009 link(s)`, then 82 `N row(s) patched` lines (16,384 apart, final group 9,905), then `patched 1337009 row(s); … still holds 1337009 row(s)`. ### Post-checks **1 — the binding gate (this is the real acceptance):** ```bash python -m Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding.site_source_pages gate \ --published ~/isasearch-published \ --artefact ~/map-artefact.json \ --namespace isasearch-2025-2-afp-2026-05-13 \ --region aws-us-west-2 --sample 500 ``` One green run binds all three: artefact ↔ published tree (via the report's `artefact_hash`) and artefact ↔ namespace (via the composed-link comparison). Expect exit 0 and, unchanged from today's tree-only run: ``` checked 15970528 reference(s); 232 site-external exempted (D50); 1530342 fragment(s) verified on 9870 page(s) coverage: positioned 99.28%, linked 99.28% of 1337009 row link(s) (9599 empty) reported, not failed (D54): 106 inherited fragment(s) … namespace sample: 500 row(s) compared, stratified gate passed: zero misses ``` Note that 8 of the 500 sampled ids have an empty composed link and therefore cannot discriminate — 492 do. **2 — cover the blind tail.** Until finding 4 is fixed, `--sample 500` never inspects the last 2,682 ids and a larger sample does not help (it can be worse). Query `ids[-1]` explicitly, or run once more with `--sample 1000` (blind tail 1,345) *in addition to* 500 — the two windows have different tails. **3 — idempotency.** Delete the checkpoint and re-run the patch. `patch_rows` writing identical values is a no-op; the second run must finish with the same before/after count and the gate must stay green. (Re-running *with* the checkpoint intact exercises the other branch: `nothing to do: the checkpoint says all 1337009 row(s) were already patched`.) **4 — one human eyeball.** Fetch one card end-to-end and click its source link. §17.7's three verified URLs are `/source/HOL.HOL.html#L513`, `/source/Forcing.Arities.html#L235`, `/source/_aux/AFP/AutoCorres2/function_pointer.ML.html#L298`. ### Residual risks I am explicitly naming, however small - The count guard proves *cardinality*, not *identity*: if the DB had gained N ids and lost N others, counts would match while N patches were silently ignored and N rows kept a null link. Mitigated by (a) `document_id`/`_hash128` being unchanged since before the export, (b) my measured 16-removed/0-added/0-changed delta, and (c) the post-patch sample, whose "fewer rows than asked for" clause catches a missing sampled id. Residual coverage: 500 of 1.3M. - Four workers declare the new `source_link` attribute in the same instant on the very first group. Documented-safe (additive, identical declaration), never observed. If it does conflict, the error is non-retryable, the checkpoint has not advanced, and resume is clean. - Nothing binds the *patch* to the published tree — only operator discipline points both at the same `--artefact`. The post-patch gate closes this, which is why post-check 1 is not optional. - turbopuffer bills by patched size (~100 MB of attribute data); a resume re-sends at most one group (16,384 rows ≈ 1.8 MB). *(Marked LOW/pedantic explicitly: findings 8, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. No spec-relaxation proposals — every finding above is either a code fix, a doc fix, or an operational precondition; none asks §17 or D49–D54 to give ground.)*

Here is the cross-examination. --- # Reviewer B — turn 2: cross-examination of Sibling A ## Consolidated verdict list ### A1 — merge title/h1 exemption is per-LINE · **CONFIRM the mechanism, DOWNGRADE HIGH → MEDIUM, ADOPT A's fix (improved)** My B8 and A1 are the same defect; A is right that I under-rated it and right about the fix shape. Evidence I ran: on all 12 real conflicts, every divergent line is line **6** or line **12**, and the residual text outside the ``/`<h1>` element on those lines is **empty string** in all 6 cases. So A's "safe today only because the renderer puts title/h1 on dedicated lines" is exactly right, and it is safe by *renderer layout*, not by the rule. Why MEDIUM and not HIGH: A's demonstration is a synthetic probe. There are **zero** real instances, the failure is confined to auxiliary pages, and it cannot touch `source_link`. HIGH is reserved for things that can go wrong on the night. **Converged fix (one shape, and it also does half of A2's job):** replace the line exemption with element-level normalisation *and* canonicalise the title in the output: ```python _TITLE_TEXT = re.compile(r"(<(title|h1)\b[^>]*>).*?(</\2>)", re.S) def _canonical_heading(line, sym): # used for BOTH the comparison and the merged output return _TITLE_TEXT.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}File ‹{sym}›{m.group(3)}", line) ``` Compare `_TAG.sub("", _canonical_heading(other, sym))` against the same for the base — no exemption at all — and emit the canonicalised line. This deletes `_TITLE_OR_H1`, deletes the exemption branch, and makes the published title a function of `sym` instead of a function of which copy won. Rewrite the single-line fixture test as a multi-line one, as A says. ### A2 — base rule anti-correlated with ownership · **CONFIRM, and I can sharpen it: A's proposed rule ordering would not fix it** This is the most important finding of either turn. Fully confirmed, with the mechanism pinned: - `HOL-Library.Word` → `./contrib/Isabelle2025-2/src/HOL/Library/Word.thy` (3,248,568 B rendered) - `Zip_Benchmarks.Word` → `./contrib/afp-2026-05-13/thys/Zippy/Zippy/Instances/Zip/Examples/Benchmarks/Word.thy` (3,543,487 B rendered) **Two different source files.** The published `_aux/ISABELLE_HOME/src/HOL/Library/Tools/smt_word.ML.html` — the HOL *Library's* own ML file — links `Word.word` **20×**, plus `ucast`, `scast`, `slice`, `word_cat`, `word_rotl/rotr`, `word_sle/sless`, all to `/source/Zip_Benchmarks.Word.html`. The losing copy resolves them to `../../../../../Word.html` (= `HOL-Library.Word`), which is correct. `word_lib.ML` is the same, 3×. The gate cannot see this: the target exists and the fragments resolve. **The sharpening — A's implied ordering (title first, then non-umbrella) does not fix it.** I measured the titles: the *broken* AFP-ALL-3 copy's title is `File ‹~~/src/HOL/Library/Tools/smt_word.ML›` (names `sym` ✓) and the *correct* HOL-Library copy's title is `File ‹Tools/smt_word.ML›` (does **not** name `sym` ✗). The current title rule picked the broken copy **because** its title names the symbolic path. Title-first keeps the bug. **Measured on all 22 groups**, the rule `prefer a copy not rendered under an umbrella build session` changes exactly **2** bases — `smt_word.ML` and `word_lib.ML` — and leaves the other 20 byte-identical: | group family | copies | effect | |---|---|---| | `~~/src/Provers/*`, `~~/src/Tools/*` (18 groups) | 1 of 2 non-umbrella | already picks the `HOL/HOL/…` copy; **unchanged** | | `smt_word.ML`, `word_lib.ML` | 1 of 2 non-umbrella | **changes — both defects fixed** | | `$AFP/Case_Labeling/util.ML` | 0 of 3 non-umbrella | rule silent; title rule correctly picks `AFP-DEP1-15`; **unchanged** | | `~~/src/Doc/antiquote_setup.ML` | 0 of 5 non-umbrella | rule silent; not a conflict; **unchanged** | Note A said "the 3"; it is **2**. `Case_Labeling/util.ML` has all three copies under the umbrella chapter and is already correct via the title rule — which is why the title criterion must be *kept*, just demoted. **Converged rule, in this order:** 1. prefer a copy **not rendered by an umbrella build session**; 2. among those, prefer one whose title names the symbolic path; 3. then sorted rendered location. With A1's canonicalisation applied, criterion 2 stops carrying any correctness weight and becomes a pure tiebreak — which is the right shape: the base copy then decides *only* which session's reference resolution the page carries, and criterion 1 decides that on the right grounds. **Caveat on the discriminator.** "Under `Unsorted/`" is the renderer's chapter for sessions declaring no chapter, which is where every umbrella build lands. Using it as a *selection* input does not violate §17.2 (which forbids umbrella names leaking into public *output*), but it is a string the classification does not currently name. The cleanest available formulation without hard-coding a build name: *the copy whose rendered session directory is a session declared by the distribution or the AFP* — `declared_sessions()` is already imported by `run_scan` and would make this a checked property rather than a path-prefix guess. That is a design choice for the user, not for me. ### A3 — D54 counts pairs, not occurrences · **CONFIRM, numbers exact** Independently reproduced over the published tree: **106** distinct `(page, fragment)` misses, **425** total reference occurrences, max **253** on one fragment — `HOL.HOL.html#offset_20940..20947` — across **15** pages, all `offset_…`. Runners-up: 12× on `HOL-Real_Asymp.Multiseries_Expansion_Bounds.html#offset_9596..9621`, 10× on `Sophie_Germain.SG_Theorem.html#offset_8708..8718`. A's 425/253 are right to the digit. A's fix (Counter, report occurrences, correct the baseline text) is right. Report **both**: "106 distinct fragments over 425 references" — the pair count is the right alarm for *how many things the renderer forgot*, the occurrence count for *how many reader clicks land wrong*. ### A4 — D54 grades by where-found · **CONFIRM (= my #9).
